# Preflight: everything in one file

> Preflight is a set of GitLab CI/CD components for Wayne State apps. Include them and your pipeline runs PROCTOR, PHP tests on each supported version, a Composer audit, an SBOM, Pint, PHPStan and ESLint.

The README and the Markdown twin of every page, joined. The index is https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt. Written by Squire's agent-ready kit; do not edit.

---

## README

Source: https://nougat.snu.gs/enterprise-apps/preflight/blob/HEAD/README.md

## Preflight

**Every push is cleared for takeoff.**

Preflight is a set of GitLab CI/CD components that give every WSU app the
same checks: PROCTOR, PHP tests on each supported version, Composer audit,
an SBOM, Pint, PHPStan and ESLint.

**Not to be confused with:** Preflight is the CI pipeline; it runs Pinstripe's style checks and PROCTOR but sets neither.

Front page: [`site/index.html`](https://nougat.snu.gs/enterprise-apps/preflight/blob/HEAD/site/index.html), a static page; see [`site/README.md`](https://nougat.snu.gs/enterprise-apps/preflight/blob/HEAD/site/README.md).
On Citadel it is served by the raw-PHP deploy layer in [`deploy/`](https://nougat.snu.gs/enterprise-apps/preflight/blob/HEAD/deploy/): a Squire kit whose front controller serves `site/` behind HELMET's security headers. For local development, keep serving `site/` directly.
Documentation: the full manual lives at [preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/).

### Where the code lives

The canonical repository is on nougat: [enterprise-apps/preflight](https://nougat.snu.gs/enterprise-apps/preflight). git.wayne.edu and GitHub ([waynestate/preflight](https://github.com/waynestate/preflight)) are read-only mirrors of it.
Open issues and merge requests on nougat, not on the mirrors.
This moves to git.wayne.edu once it has CI runners. Cleared for takeoff from nougat; the mirrors are just other gates.

Components are GA on the Free tier since GitLab 17.0. They work only within
the same GitLab instance that hosts this project.

### Components

#### proctor

Runs `vendor/bin/proctor check --format=codequality` and publishes the
result as a GitLab Code Quality report. The job installs the app's
dependencies with `composer install --no-plugins --no-scripts`, so the
app's plugins and scripts never run inside the job.

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/proctor@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      proctor_command: vendor/bin/proctor check --format=codequality
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
|-------|------|---------|--------------|
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `proctor` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `php:8.4-cli-trixie@sha256:9cf851bc2c1b37c3e59dfd677a3c3e56d485af5a47c93f629424bb039eafcb69` | Docker image for the job. |
| `composer_version` | string | `2.10.3` | Composer version to install. |
| `allow_failure` | boolean | `false` | Whether the job can fail without failing the pipeline. |
| `proctor_command` | string | `vendor/bin/proctor check --format=codequality` | The proctor command to run. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run the command in, relative to the project root. |

#### php-test

Runs the test command on each supported PHP version through `parallel:matrix`.

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      test_command: vendor/bin/phpunit
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
|-------|------|---------|--------------|
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the jobs. |
| `job_name` | string | `php-test` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `php:${PHP_VERSION}-cli-trixie` | Docker image for the jobs. The default carries the literal `${PHP_VERSION}`, which GitLab expands in the image at job time. |
| `php_versions` | array | `["8.3", "8.4", "8.5"]` | PHP versions to test against. |
| `composer_version` | string | `2.10.3` | Composer version to install. |
| `test_command` | string | `vendor/bin/phpunit` | The test command to run. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run the command in, relative to the project root. |

##### Caching

The jobs always cache Composer downloads in `.composer-cache/` so repeat runs
do not re-download every package. The cache key depends on `composer.lock`
and is prefixed with the PHP version, so a dependency change invalidates the
cache and each PHP version gets its own cache.

##### Try the next PHP release without breaking the pipeline

Include `php-test` a second time for the release that is not supported yet, name that job, and let it fail. The name
is what lets your own `.gitlab-ci.yml` loosen only that job:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@<full commit SHA> # <tag>
    inputs:
      php_versions: ["8.6"]
      job_name: php-test-next
      # While 8.6 only has release candidate images, name the tag: php:${PHP_VERSION}-rc-cli-trixie
      # image: "php:${PHP_VERSION}-rc-cli-trixie"

php-test-next:
  allow_failure: true
```

A red `php-test-next` job is an early warning, not a stop. Drop the `allow_failure` and move the version into the main
`php_versions` list once the release is supported (the supported versions follow `policy.json`).

#### composer-audit

Runs `composer audit --locked` and fails on advisories.

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/composer-audit@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      working_dir: .
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
|-------|------|---------|--------------|
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `composer-audit` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `composer:2@sha256:b6dcd72ca98fa19d0e5b8476de179859704891fad06dd9e0b96833d4c430a5fc` | Docker image for the job. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run composer audit in, relative to the project root. |

##### Run it on a schedule

New advisories are published after code is merged, so a green pipeline today
can be stale tomorrow. Create a weekly pipeline schedule on the default
branch: project settings, Build, Pipeline schedules. The component needs
nothing extra; it carries no `rules:` block, so it runs in scheduled
pipelines like any other. Creating the schedule is a project setting, not a
file in the app's repo, and someone with Maintainer rights on the app must
do it. It is the one preflight check that books its own flight time.

#### sbom

Generates a CycloneDX SBOM with `cyclonedx/cyclonedx-php-composer`, validates it, and publishes it as an artifact. The plugin is installed globally, so the app's `composer.json` is never touched.

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/sbom@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      output: sbom.cdx.json
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
|-------|------|---------|--------------|
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `sbom` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `composer:2.10.3@sha256:b6dcd72ca98fa19d0e5b8476de179859704891fad06dd9e0b96833d4c430a5fc` | Docker image for the job. |
| `omit_dev` | boolean | `true` | Whether to omit dev dependencies from the SBOM. |
| `output` | string | `sbom.cdx.json` | Path of the SBOM file to publish, relative to the project root. It must be a relative path; GitLab refuses the pipeline at creation if it is not. |

#### pint

Version 1 · Category: Testing/Validation · Tags: php,style,pint

Runs the app's own [Laravel Pint](https://laravel.com/docs/12.x/pint) in test mode and fails the pipeline on style errors. The app must require `laravel/pint` as a dev dependency and ship a `pint.json` (or point `config` at its own file).

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/pint@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      config: pint.json
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
|-------|------|---------|--------------|
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `pint` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `composer:2.10.3@sha256:b6dcd72ca98fa19d0e5b8476de179859704891fad06dd9e0b96833d4c430a5fc` | Docker image for the job. |
| `config` | string | `pint.json` | Path to the app's Pint config file. It must be a relative path; GitLab refuses the pipeline at creation if it is not. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run Pint in, relative to the project root. |

#### phpstan

Version 1 · Category: Testing/Validation · Tags: php,static-analysis,phpstan

Runs the app's own [PHPStan](https://phpstan.org/) and fails the pipeline on static analysis errors, writing a GitLab Code Quality report. The app must require `phpstan/phpstan` as a dev dependency and ship a `phpstan.neon` (or point `config` at its own file).

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/phpstan@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      config: phpstan.neon
      memory_limit: 1G
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
|-------|------|---------|--------------|
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `phpstan` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `composer:2.10.3@sha256:b6dcd72ca98fa19d0e5b8476de179859704891fad06dd9e0b96833d4c430a5fc` | Docker image for the job. |
| `config` | string | `phpstan.neon` | Path to the app's PHPStan config file. It must be a relative path; GitLab refuses the pipeline at creation if it is not. |
| `memory_limit` | string | `1G` | Memory limit passed to PHPStan. A PHP size such as `1G`, `512M` or `-1`; GitLab refuses the pipeline at creation if it is not. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run PHPStan in, relative to the project root. |

#### eslint

Version 1 · Category: Testing/Validation · Tags: javascript,style,eslint,prettier

Runs the app's own [ESLint](https://eslint.org/) (and [Prettier](https://prettier.io/)) and fails the pipeline on lint or format errors. The app must require `@waynestate/pinstripe`, `eslint` and `prettier` as dev dependencies and ship an `eslint.config.js` (or point `eslint_args` at its own files).

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/eslint@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      eslint_args: .
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
|-------|------|---------|--------------|
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `eslint` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `node:22.13-alpine@sha256:e2b39f7b64281324929257d0f8004fb6cb4bf0fdfb9aa8cedb235a766aec31da` | Docker image for the job. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run the commands in, relative to the project root. |
| `eslint_args` | string | `.` | Arguments passed to eslint. |
| `prettier` | boolean | `true` | Whether to also run `prettier --check`. |

#### package-publish

Version 1 · Category: Release/Publishing · Tags: composer,publish,release

Publishes a semantic version tag to the GitLab group's built-in Composer
registry. The job runs only on tags, reads the registry first, and refuses a
moved version: a version already published from this commit passes quietly,
and a version published from a different commit fails the pipeline, because
GitLab would otherwise overwrite it without a word. The default image ships
curl and PHP, which the job uses for the registry round trip.

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/package-publish@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      group_id: "<your group id>"
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
|-------|------|---------|--------------|
| `stage` | string | `deploy` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `package-publish` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `composer:2.10.3@sha256:b6dcd72ca98fa19d0e5b8476de179859704891fad06dd9e0b96833d4c430a5fc` | Docker image for the job. The default ships curl and PHP, which the job uses for the registry round trip. |
| `group_id` | string | none | Numeric id of the GitLab group whose built-in Composer registry hosts the package. Required. |
| `read_token_variable` | string | `PACKAGE_READ_TOKEN` | Name of the masked CI variable holding a token with the `read_package_registry` scope, used to read the registry before publishing. |

Protect your release tags.

#### renovate

Runs [Renovate](https://docs.renovatebot.com/) as a scheduled or manual job
that bumps image digests, GitHub action SHAs and package versions across the
group's repositories, and merges the green ones itself. Bumps of `component:`
include pins are covered by the preset and wait for review. Majors open a
merge request and wait for a person. See [Renovate](#renovate) for what
auto-merges and what waits.

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/renovate@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      git_author: "Preflight Bot <preflight-bot@example.com>"
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
|-------|------|---------|--------------|
| `job_name` | string | `renovate` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `renovate/renovate:44.192.2@sha256:37960a62ba1faa9079a7c4eead9b3f4470748a64ecd207e06c09fd8858673e17` | Docker image for the job. |
| `autodiscover_filter` | string | `$CI_PROJECT_NAMESPACE/*` | Glob limiting which projects Renovate discovers, relative to the runner project's namespace. |
| `dry_run` | string | `"null"` | Dry run mode: `null` (disabled), `lookup` or `full`. |
| `git_author` | string | none | Author of the commits and merge requests Renovate creates, in the form `Name `. Required. |

#### portability

Proves the app image meets the twelve-factor boot contract. It builds the
image with Buildah (no Docker daemon, no elevated runner), boots it the
strict way, and validates it with goss: the health path answers 200 for a
foreign Host, the root filesystem and the app root are not writable, the app
runs as the declared uid, and each declared writable path is writable. No
takeoff without a clean pre-flight.

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/portability@<full-commit-sha> # <tag, once one ships>
    inputs:
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
      context: .
      start_command: php -S 0.0.0.0:8080 -t public
```

Portability ships in 0.1.4 and later (0.1.3 does not include it), so pin the
`0.1.4` tag, or the full commit SHA of a commit at or after it. The build job needs a runner that permits
user namespaces (Buildah uses unshare for its storage); the run job needs only
the project's container registry and an app image that carries curl, sha256sum
and tar.

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
|-------|------|---------|--------------|
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the portability jobs. |
| `image` | string | `$CI_REGISTRY_IMAGE/portability:$CI_COMMIT_SHORT_SHA` | App image the portability-run job starts and validates. The default is what portability-build pushes; GitLab expands the CI variables at job time. |
| `buildah_image` | string | `quay.io/buildah/stable:v1.43.5-immutable@sha256:7c2b605262748ace2c5c57c5550942d0adad57aec82ede3070927722306c0ffb` | Buildah image for the portability-build job; it builds and pushes the app image. |
| `dockerfile` | string | `Dockerfile` | Dockerfile to build, relative to the context. |
| `context` | string | `.` | Build context, relative to the project root. |
| `app_root` | string | `/app` | Directory inside the image where the app lives. |
| `writable_paths` | array | `["storage", "bootstrap/cache"]` | Paths the app may write to, relative to app_root. Each must be writable by the app user. |
| `port` | number | `8080` | Port the app listens on inside the container. |
| `health_path` | string | `/up` | Path the app must answer 200 on for any Host. |
| `uid` | number | `100123` | Numeric uid the app runs as. The gid is always 0. |
| `start_command` | string | none | Command that starts the app inside the image. It is app-specific, so it is required and has no default. |
| `boot_timeout` | number | `60` | Seconds goss retries the health check while the app boots. |

The default is an immutable tag (`-immutable`) pinned by digest, because the plain version tag can be re-pushed and its old digest removed.

### Same instance only

Components work only inside the GitLab instance that hosts this project.
Components cannot be used across instances except by mirroring.

### GitHub mirrors

Components work only inside one GitLab instance, so a package that is also
mirrored to `github.com/waynestate` cannot include them there. For those
mirrors, Preflight ships a reusable GitHub Actions workflow that runs the same
checks: the package's `composer ci` script on each supported PHP version, plus
a Composer audit.

Each package keeps its checks in a `ci` script in its `composer.json`; the
workflow just calls `composer ci`, so the mirror runs whatever the package
already runs on GitLab.

The workflow lives at `.github/workflows/php-package.yml` in this repo. A
mirrored package calls it from its own `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

```yaml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: ['**']
    tags: ['v*', '*.*.*']

jobs:
  ci:
    uses: waynestate/preflight/.github/workflows/php-package.yml@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
```

This workflow ships in the `0.1.1` tag, so pin the full commit SHA of the
release tag and keep the tag in a trailing comment. A tag or branch can move;
a SHA cannot. PROCTOR's `preflight-pinned` check warns when an include is not
pinned to a commit SHA. The Renovate preset (see the Renovate section)
proposes the bumps, and they wait for review (the `needs-review` label).

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
|-------|------|---------|--------------|
| `php-versions` | string (JSON array) | `'["8.3","8.4","8.5"]'` | PHP versions to test, lowest first. The audit job runs on the first entry. |
| `ci-command` | string | `composer ci` | The command to run in each PHP version job. |
| `working-directory` | string | `.` | Directory to run the command in, relative to the repository root. |

The workflow is committed to this repo (and so to GitLab) but only runs on the
GitHub mirror; GitLab ignores `.github/workflows`. A release tag is not done
until it is green on both sides. Two cockpits, one checklist.

### Renovate

Preflight owns the stack's version automation (ADR-0015): the shared preset
[`renovate/default.json`](https://nougat.snu.gs/enterprise-apps/preflight/blob/HEAD/renovate/default.json) and the
[`renovate` component](#renovate) that runs it. A private runner project
includes the component on a schedule; Renovate discovers every repository in
the filter, opens merge requests for outdated versions, and GitLab's native
auto-merge takes in the ones whose pipeline is green.

Every stack repository carries a `renovate.json` that extends the shared
preset, so the rules change in one place:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://docs.renovatebot.com/renovate-schema.json",
  "extends": ["local>enterprise-apps/preflight//renovate/default"]
}
```

#### What auto-merges

Digest updates, pin and pinDigest updates, and patch and minor version bumps
auto-merge when the pipeline is green. Lock file maintenance runs weekly and
auto-merges the same way. Every merge request carries the `auto-deps` label.
The exception is Preflight's own pins: an update that touches the templates,
the contract or this repository's own pipeline, a bump of a component include
version, and a bump of the recorded Squire kit version, never auto-merge (see
What waits for review). One image gets a narrower rule: `quay.io/buildah/stable`
only ever matches `-immutable` tags, because Red Hat re-pushed a mutable tag
and garbage-collected the old digest, which broke an image job.

#### What waits

Major version bumps never auto-merge. The merge request carries the `major`
label and waits for a person.

#### What waits for review

Updates that change an image digest inside the templates, the contract, or
this repository's own pipeline, bumps of a Preflight component version in an
app's `component:` include, and bumps of the recorded Squire kit version
(labeled `squire-kit`) carry the `needs-review` label and never auto-merge.
They wait for a person because those pins are what every app pipeline runs:
a changed digest here changes what every consuming pipeline executes, so it
earns a human eye even when its own pipeline is green. The Squire kit version
bump is refreshed by a person who runs `squire update` (with the right path
for the repo), reviews the diff and commits it to the branch; the runner runs
no commands, so the merge request carries no postUpgradeTasks.

#### Why MySQL and HA-Proxy get digests only

The `mysql` and `haproxy` images mirror the versions Citadel actually runs,
not the newest releases in the world. Bumping their tags would drift the apps
away from production, so only digest updates are enabled for them: the same
tag, the exact image. `citadel/php-apache` is disabled entirely, because
Squire's own data owns that image.

#### Set up (the user does this)

This repository ships the preset and the component, and creates nothing else.
A person must set up:

- A private runner project that includes the `renovate` component on a
  schedule (see The runner project).
- The `RENOVATE_TOKEN` masked CI variable in that project, and optionally
  `GITHUB_COM_TOKEN`.
- A pipeline schedule on that project so the job runs regularly; weekly on
  Monday is a sensible default.

#### The runner project

The runner project must stay private. It holds `RENOVATE_TOKEN`, a token that
can open and merge merge requests across the group, and this repository is
mirrored to public GitHub. Use a group bot account for the token, not a
person's: the bot outlives any one maintainer, and the commits keep one
stable author.

| Variable | Required | What it does |
|----------|----------|--------------|
| `RENOVATE_TOKEN` | yes | Masked CI variable in the runner project; the job reads it straight from the project, the component does not map it. A project access token with Developer, or Maintainer where only Maintainers may merge. |
| `GITHUB_COM_TOKEN` | no | Masked CI variable in the runner project; the job reads it straight from the project, the component does not map it. Lookups against github.com do not hit anonymous rate limits. |

Do not add `RENOVATE_TOKEN: $RENOVATE_TOKEN` to your own `variables:`; that self-reference arrives as literal text.

The component writes its `config.js` at job time, so the `registryAliases`
entry for the GitLab instance comes from the predefined `CI_SERVER_FQDN`
variable. No hostname is stored in this repository.

### Keep the job token allowlist short

An app that installs private packages from GitLab's package registry should
list only the projects it really needs in its CI/CD job token allowlist
(project settings, Settings, CI/CD, Job token permissions), use the
fine-grained permissions where they fit, and review the list when a
dependency is dropped. A leaked job token acts with the triggering user's
access. This is a project setting, not a file Preflight can create or check.

### When the components run

The components are ordinary jobs, so they run whenever the app's pipeline
runs. To run them on every merge request and on pushes to the default
branch, put a `workflow:rules` block in the app's own `.gitlab-ci.yml`:

```yaml
workflow:
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH

include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/proctor@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/composer-audit@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/sbom@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/pint@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/phpstan@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/eslint@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
```

The `workflow:rules` block must live in the app's own file. A component
cannot set the pipeline's `workflow:rules` for the project that includes it,
so the `merge_request_event` rule goes in the app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`.

### What the components cannot force

An included component is a set of ordinary jobs. The app's own `.gitlab-ci.yml` is merged over them, so an app can
override a job's keys, skip it with `rules`, or delete the `include:` line. Preflight makes the safe pipeline the easy
one; it does not lock it. Rollcall is where skipped or weakened gates will show up. A preflight checklist only works
if the pilot reads it.

#### Which jobs may be allowed to fail

Only `proctor` takes an `allow_failure` input (default `false`). A policy finding is a warning while an app adopts
PROCTOR's rules, so the job may fail without failing the pipeline during adoption. `composer-audit` has no such input
on purpose: a known advisory must fail the pipeline. The other jobs have no `allow_failure` input either.

No template adds a global key such as `default:`, `variables:`, `workflow:` or `stages:`. `tests/check-contract.sh`
(and its `.ps1` twin) fails on any top-level key in a template that is not a job named in `contract/inputs.json`, so a
global key fails `composer ci`.

#### Protection checklist

A pilot signs each line of the checklist; the plane does not sign for you. Five project settings make the gates
harder to skip, and every one of them works on GitLab Community Edition:

- [ ] **Protect the default branch** and require a merge request to change it. Every change to `.gitlab-ci.yml` then
  gets a reviewer. (Code owner approval needs Premium, so on Community Edition the reviewer is whoever merges.)
- [ ] **Protect the release tags.** Protect `*` or the release tag pattern so only maintainers can create or move a
  tag. A component ref is a tag, so whoever can move it controls every pipeline that pins it.
- [ ] **Set merge request approvals to at least one** for changes to the default branch. Approvals are available on
  every tier, but code owner rules within them need Premium, so on Community Edition the approval rests with whoever
  has merge rights: rely on the merger as the reviewer.
- [ ] **Set "Minimum role to use pipeline variables" to `no_one_allowed`** unless the project needs pipeline variables.
  The components take inputs, which are fixed and type checked for the whole run. Self-managed GitLab defaults this
  setting to `maintainer`.
- [ ] **Keep secrets away from fork merge requests.** A fork's merge request pipeline runs the fork's configuration.
  Review a fork's `.gitlab-ci.yml` before running its pipeline, and never give it protected variables.

These are project settings Preflight cannot create or check, and a read-only token drift report was considered and
left out on purpose: it would trade a token for a warning, and the checklist costs nothing to keep.

### Strongly recommended: a git.wayne.edu instance runner.

Until git.wayne.edu has a runner, CI runs on the GitLab instance that has one, and Preflight and each
app must live on or be mirrored to it. A git.wayne.edu instance runner is strongly recommended. Ask
for a non-privileged Docker executor (no privileged mode, no Docker socket mount), a fresh ephemeral
environment for every job, and no shell executor shared between projects; capacity and maintenance
stay with ops. A job that needs the host's Docker socket to take off has skipped its own preflight.

### Include a component twice

Every component except `portability` takes a `job_name` input, whose default is the job's usual name. Set it when one
project includes the same component more than once, for example in a monorepo with two apps; without it the two jobs
would share a name and merge into one.

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/pint@<full commit SHA> # <tag>
    inputs:
      working_dir: app
      job_name: pint-app
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/pint@<full commit SHA> # <tag>
    inputs:
      working_dir: admin
      job_name: pint-admin
```

`job_name` ships in 0.1.4, so pin 0.1.4 or a SHA at or after that release. `portability` keeps its two fixed
job names, because `portability-run` waits on `portability-build`.

### Shared conventions

- Composer vendor: `waynestate/`
- License: MIT
- PHP floor: `^8.3`
- JavaScript components install with `npm ci --ignore-scripts`. The job carries no token beyond `CI_JOB_TOKEN` (BEST_PRACTICES.md 4.12).
- Path-like inputs (`config` on phpstan and pint, `output` on sbom) must be relative paths, and `memory_limit` (phpstan) takes a PHP size such as `1G`, `512M` or `-1`. Each carries an input `regex`, so GitLab refuses the pipeline at creation when a value does not match.

### Updating image pins

Every image the components run is pinned by digest (`name:tag@sha256:...`),
so a repointed tag cannot quietly change what a pipeline executes. The tag
stays in front of the digest so a diff still reads like a version bump.

The php-test matrix is the one exception. Its PHP images are tag-pinned on
purpose, so those jobs run on the newest PHP patch release; every other
component image is digest-pinned.

To look up the digest for an image:

```sh
docker buildx imagetools inspect <image>:<tag>
```

Use the top-level `Digest:` line (the multi-arch index digest), not a
per-platform one. Without `buildx`, `docker manifest inspect -v :`
shows the same index digest.

Pins change only through a reviewed merge request.

### Template lint

`composer ci` runs `bin/lint-templates` before the fixture tests. The lint scans
`templates/**/*.yml` and `.github/workflows/*.yml` for unsafe CI patterns:

- `privileged`: `privileged: true`
- `dind-service`: Docker-in-Docker services
- `docker-sock`: references to `docker.sock`
- `kaniko-image`: Kaniko images
- `unpinned-action`: GitHub `uses:` entries that are not pinned to a 40-character SHA
- `image-no-tag` and `image-latest`: image references with no tag or with `latest`
- `image-no-digest`: a warning for a tagged image that is not pinned by digest

The container-build rules (`privileged`, `dind-service`, `docker-sock` and `kaniko-image`) are explained in
BEST_PRACTICES.md 4.17.

Known warnings can be allowlisted in `lint-allow.yml`. Each entry needs `file`,
`rule` and `reason`; the reason is required so an allowlist entry is a reviewed
decision, not a silence. The preflight checklist checks the checklist.

### Proof

Proof runs against real Wayne State applications are on a private site, [proof.apps.wayne.edu/preflight](https://proof.apps.wayne.edu/preflight/), behind a Wayne State employee sign-in.

### Docs

The full documentation lives at [preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/) on the project site, built from `docs/` by Squire's docs builder. It starts with the overview page; the rest of the manual follows as the pages are written.

- `composer docs` rebuilds `site/docs/` from `docs/`; run it after editing a page.
- `composer docs:check` fails when the built site is stale; `composer ci` runs it.

The pages are committed because the deploy server serves `site/` without building. Every page links back to its Markdown, and the footer stamps the version the docs describe. Cleared for takeoff: the flight manual flies with the aircraft.

### Local checks

Maintainers: how to build, test and release this project, and where its data comes from, is in [MAINTAINING.md](https://nougat.snu.gs/enterprise-apps/preflight/blob/HEAD/MAINTAINING.md).

Run the template lint and the fixture tests with Docker:

```sh
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd):/app" -w /app composer:2 composer install
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd):/app" -w /app composer:2 composer ci
```

In PowerShell, use `${PWD}` instead of `$(pwd)`:

```powershell
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2 composer install
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2 composer ci
```

Run the PHP fixture app separately:

```sh
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)/tests/fixture-app:/app" -w /app composer:2 composer install
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)/tests/fixture-app:/app" -w /app php:8.4-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
```

Run the portability fixtures with Docker; they build and boot the three
fixtures under `tests/portability` the strict way and exit 0 only when `good`
passes and both `bad-*` fixtures fail:

```sh
sh tests/check-portability.sh
```

```powershell
pwsh -File tests/check-portability.ps1
```

### The cast

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/

Wayne State app stack · CI templates

## Preflight

Every push is cleared for takeoff.

pre·flight noun The checklist a pilot runs before takeoff. Every push runs this one before Citadel.

Preflight is a set of GitLab CI/CD components. Add them to the `include:` block in your `.gitlab-ci.yml` and your pipeline runs PROCTOR, PHP tests on each supported version, a Composer audit, an SBOM, Pint, PHPStan and ESLint, the same way the other stack apps do.

.gitlab-ci.yml

```
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
```

Already included in [WELD](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/) and in every [Sourdough](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/) app. Use Preflight on its own to give a GitLab project you already have the stack's CI checks.

[Run the checklist](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/#checklist) [File a flight plan](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/#flight-plan)

![Preflight mark: a runway in perspective with a gold centerline](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/brand/preflight-avatar-512.png)

Normal procedures

### Before takeoff

These are the jobs the components add to your app's own pipeline, in the order the card lists them. Scroll, and it runs itself.

WSU app stack · normal checklist

Before takeoff · every push

1. PROCTOR Checked
   Checks the app against the stack's standards and publishes the result as a GitLab Code Quality report.
   `vendor/bin/proctor check --format=codequality`
2. PHP tests 8.3 · 8.4 · 8.5 pass
   One job per supported PHP version, through `parallel:matrix`. End-of-life PHP is not on the list.
   `vendor/bin/phpunit`
3. Composer audit No advisories
   Audits the exact versions in `composer.lock` and fails the pipeline on a known advisory.
   `composer audit --locked`
4. SBOM Validated
   A CycloneDX bill of materials, validated and kept as a job artifact. The app's `composer.json` is never touched.
   `composer CycloneDX:make-sbom --output-format=JSON --validate`
5. Pint Clean
   The app's own Laravel Pint, in test mode, with the app's own `pint.json`.
   `vendor/bin/pint --test --config=pint.json`
6. PHPStan No errors
   The app's own PHPStan, writing its findings as a Code Quality report.
   `vendor/bin/phpstan analyse --error-format=gitlab`
7. ESLint · Prettier Clean
   The app's own ESLint and `prettier --check`, installed from the lock with scripts off.
   `npx --no-install eslint .`
8. Clearance Cleared for takeoff
   Every gate green. The release is free to leave for Citadel.

Checklist complete. Tray tables up, tests green.

- PROCTOR
- PHP 8.3
- PHP 8.4
- PHP 8.5
- AUDIT
- SBOM
- PINT
- PHPSTAN
- ESLINT
- A11Ycoming soon
- CONTRACTcoming soon
- FRESHNESScoming soon
- CLEARED FOR TAKEOFF

Makes the Composer audit fail, to show the pipeline holding short.

Cockpit placards

### Seven checks, one include each

Each one is an ordinary GitLab job with typed inputs, and the defaults below are what you get if you set nothing. All seven are in the 0.1.4 tag, so pin the full commit SHA of the release tag, with the tag in a comment. Two more components, `package-publish` and `renovate`, ship in the same tag; the README documents them.

in 0.1.4

#### proctor

Watches the cabin.

Runs PROCTOR's checks and publishes them as a Code Quality report.

```
- component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/proctor@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
```

**6 inputs**

- **stage**: `test`
- **image**: `php:8.4-cli-trixie@sha256:…`
- **composer_version**: `2.10.3`
- **allow_failure**: `false`
- **proctor_command**: `vendor/bin/proctor check --format=codequality`
- **working_dir**: `.`

in 0.1.4

#### php-test

Three engines, all running.

The test command on each supported PHP version, one job per version.

```
- component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
```

**6 inputs**

- **stage**: `test`
- **image**: `php:${PHP_VERSION}-cli-trixie`
- **php_versions**: `["8.3", "8.4", "8.5"]`
- **composer_version**: `2.10.3`
- **test_command**: `vendor/bin/phpunit`
- **working_dir**: `.`

in 0.1.4

#### composer-audit

Checks the passenger list.

`composer audit --locked`, failing on any advisory.

```
- component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/composer-audit@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
```

**3 inputs**

- **stage**: `test`
- **image**: `composer:2@sha256:…`
- **working_dir**: `.`

in 0.1.4

#### sbom

The cargo manifest.

A validated CycloneDX SBOM, published as an artifact. The plugin installs globally, so the app's files stay as they are.

```
- component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/sbom@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
```

**4 inputs**

- **stage**: `test`
- **image**: `composer:2.10.3@sha256:…`
- **omit_dev**: `true`
- **output**: `sbom.cdx.json`

in 0.1.4

#### pint

Uniform pressed.

The app's own Laravel Pint in test mode. The app requires `laravel/pint` and ships a `pint.json`.

```
- component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/pint@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
```

**4 inputs**

- **stage**: `test`
- **image**: `composer:2.10.3@sha256:…`
- **config**: `pint.json`
- **working_dir**: `.`

in 0.1.4

#### phpstan

Instruments cross-checked.

The app's own PHPStan, with a Code Quality report. The app requires `phpstan/phpstan` and ships a `phpstan.neon`.

```
- component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/phpstan@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
```

**5 inputs**

- **stage**: `test`
- **image**: `composer:2.10.3@sha256:…`
- **config**: `phpstan.neon`
- **memory_limit**: `1G`
- **working_dir**: `.`

in 0.1.4

#### eslint

The front cabin, too.

The app's own ESLint and Prettier. The app requires `@waynestate/pinstripe`, `eslint` and `prettier`.

```
- component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/eslint@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
```

**5 inputs**

- **stage**: `test`
- **image**: `node:22.13-alpine@sha256:…`
- **working_dir**: `.`
- **eslint_args**: `.`
- **prettier**: `true`

in 0.1.4

#### php-package.yml

Two cockpits, one checklist.

Components stay inside one GitLab instance, so GitHub mirrors call this reusable workflow instead: `composer ci` on each PHP version, then a Composer audit.

```
uses: waynestate/preflight/.github/workflows/php-package.yml@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
```

**3 inputs**

- **php-versions**: `'["8.3","8.4","8.5"]'`
- **ci-command**: `composer ci`
- **working-directory**: `.`

Quick start

### File a flight plan

Box 1 is the one every app needs: after it, merge requests and pushes to the default branch run the checklist. The other three cover project settings, GitHub mirrors and running Preflight's own checks.

1 Route · `.gitlab-ci.yml`

#### Include the components

The `workflow:rules` block has to live in the app's own file: a component cannot set when the pipeline runs.

```
workflow:
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH

include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/proctor@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/composer-audit@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/sbom@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/pint@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/phpstan@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/eslint@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
```

2 Switches · project settings

#### Three settings that make gates harder to skip

All three work on GitLab Community Edition. Flip each one as you set it.

0 of 3 set

3 Alternate · GitHub mirror

#### Mirrored to GitHub? Same checks there

A package mirrored to `github.com/waynestate` keeps its checks in a `ci` script in `composer.json` and calls the reusable workflow from `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. A release tag is not done until it is green on both sides.

```
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: ['**']
    tags: ['v*', '*.*.*']

jobs:
  ci:
    uses: waynestate/preflight/.github/workflows/php-package.yml@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
```

4 Ground check · your machine

#### Run Preflight's own checks locally

From a clone of this repo: the template lint, its fixture tests, Pint and PHPStan through `composer ci`, then the inputs contract.

**Windows**

PowerShell 7. `composer ci` needs PHP 8.3+ and Composer; the contract check runs yq in Docker.

```
PS> composer install
PS> composer ci
PS> pwsh -File tests/check-contract.ps1
```

No PHP on the machine? Docker does it:

```
PS> docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2 composer install
PS> docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2 composer ci
```

**macOS · Linux**

`composer ci` needs PHP 8.3+ and Composer; the contract check needs yq v4.

```
$ composer install
$ composer ci
$ sh tests/check-contract.sh
```

No PHP on the machine? Docker does it:

```
$ docker run --rm -v "$(pwd):/app" -w /app composer:2 composer install
$ docker run --rm -v "$(pwd):/app" -w /app composer:2 composer ci
```

Crew resource management

### Hand it to your copilot

Three prompts for the coding agent you already fly with. Copy one, or run it straight in OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex or ChatGPT. Each one points the agent at Preflight's docs, lists what it must not assume, and tells it to ask you before it guesses.

#### Get started with Preflight

The agent writes your app's `.gitlab-ci.yml` with the components that fit it, whether it's raw PHP, Laravel with Blade, or Laravel with Inertia and Vue.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent adding Preflight to the GitLab pipeline of the app in this folder, at Wayne State University. Preflight is the CI of WELD, the Wayne State application stack: GitLab CI/CD components (proctor, php-test, composer-audit, sbom, pint, phpstan, eslint) that give every app the same checks, one include line each.

Read first:
- https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, the index of Preflight's pages, each one as Markdown. Fetch the pages you need; do not work from memory.
- This app's .gitlab-ci.yml if there is one, composer.json and composer.lock, and package.json with its lock file if there is one.
- ADVISOR, the stack's MCP server, if it is connected: read_project_docs for preflight, and run_proctor_check to see what the proctor job will report. If it is not connected, say so and work from the pages. How to add it: https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt

Task:
1. Say which kind of app this is: raw PHP, raw PHP with Vue, Laravel with Blade, or Laravel with Inertia and Vue.
2. Pick the components that fit, and say why for each one left out. Each has a precondition: proctor needs waynestate/proctor as a dev dependency; pint needs laravel/pint and a pint.json; phpstan needs phpstan/phpstan and a phpstan.neon; eslint needs a package.json with @waynestate/pinstripe, eslint and prettier.
3. Write the include block, every component pinned to the release Preflight's page gives today, and the workflow:rules block (merge request pipelines, and pushes to the default branch) in the app's own .gitlab-ci.yml.
4. Keep every job the file already has. Show me the whole diff before you write it.

Constraints:
- Components work only inside the GitLab instance that hosts Preflight. If this app lives on another instance, stop and say so.
- Pin every component to a released version, never a branch. Never override a component's image with an unpinned one.
- A component is not a lock: never skip or weaken a job with rules or allow_failure to get a green pipeline. Fix the finding, or ask me.
- Strongly recommended: a git.wayne.edu instance runner. Say whether this project has one, or that you cannot tell.
- Ask me before you guess, and before you push anything.

Output: the app kind, the components with a reason each, the diff, then your questions.
```

#### Or file for another route

#### Preflight on a package's GitHub mirror

Components can't leave their GitLab instance, so a `waynestate/` package mirrored to GitHub calls Preflight's reusable workflow instead.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent wiring the GitHub mirror of the Composer package in this folder into Preflight, the CI of WELD, the Wayne State application stack. GitLab is the primary; the GitHub copy is a release mirror, and GitLab components cannot run there, so Preflight ships a reusable GitHub Actions workflow that runs the same checks.

Read first:
- https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, then the GitHub mirrors section of Preflight's README (llms-full.txt carries it).
- This package's composer.json (its scripts, above all ci), .gitlab-ci.yml and .github/workflows/ if they exist.
- ADVISOR, the stack's MCP server, if it is connected: read_project_docs for preflight. If it is not connected, say so and work from the pages.

Task:
1. Check that composer.json has a ci script that runs every check the GitLab pipeline runs. The workflow only calls `composer ci`, so anything missing from the script is missing on GitHub.
2. Write .github/workflows/ci.yml that calls waynestate/preflight/.github/workflows/php-package.yml at the release Preflight's page gives today, on pushes to every branch and on release tags.
3. Set php-versions only if the package needs something other than the default. Show me the whole file before you write it.

Constraints:
- Pin the workflow to the release's full commit SHA, with the tag in a comment: PROCTOR's ci-pipelines check warns on any other uses: ref. If you cannot find the SHA, use the tag and say so.
- Never push to GitHub directly: the mirror fills from GitLab. Commit on GitLab only.
- A release tag is not done until it is green on both sides.
- Ask me before you guess, and before you push anything.

Output: the ci script as it stands and anything it lacks, the workflow file, then your questions.
```

#### Version upkeep with Preflight's Renovate preset

One `renovate.json` that extends the shared preset. Patch and minor updates merge themselves when the pipeline is green; majors wait for a person.

A prompt for your coding agent. Copy it as it stands:

```text
You are a coding agent putting the repository in this folder on Preflight's shared Renovate preset. Preflight owns the version automation of WELD, the Wayne State application stack: one preset, renovate/default.json in Preflight, and a renovate component that a private runner project runs on a schedule.

Read first:
- https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt, then the Renovate section of Preflight's README (llms-full.txt carries it): what auto-merges, what waits, and why MySQL and HA-Proxy get digests only.
- This repository's renovate.json if there is one, and its .gitlab-ci.yml.
- ADVISOR, the stack's MCP server, if it is connected: read_project_docs for preflight. If it is not connected, say so and work from the pages.

Task:
1. Add or replace renovate.json with the one the README gives: the Renovate schema, and extends set to local>enterprise-apps/preflight//renovate/default.
2. If the existing file has rules of its own, list them and ask me which to keep. Keep none silently.
3. Say what will auto-merge here and what will wait, from the preset's rules and this repository's dependencies.

Constraints:
- Change only renovate.json. Never set up a runner project, a schedule or a token: the runner project is private and holds a group-wide token. Ask me whether this group already runs one.
- Auto-merge needs a pipeline that really tests the change. If this repository has no pipeline, say so first.
- Ask me before you guess, and before you push anything.

Output: the renovate.json, what auto-merges and what waits, then your questions.
```

The agent reads the same pages you do: [llms.txt](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt) lists them, [llms-full.txt](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/llms-full.txt) holds them in one file, and this page has a [Markdown twin](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/index.md). Nothing here phones home; the buttons only copy text or open the tool you picked. You have control.

From the flight manual

### Read before flight

The limits of a shared CI template, and how Preflight checks its own.

Warning

**A component is not a lock.** An app's own `.gitlab-ci.yml` is merged over the included jobs, so it can override a job's keys, skip it with `rules`, or delete the `include:` line. Preflight makes the safe pipeline the easy one; Rollcall is where skipped or weakened gates show up.

A preflight checklist only works if the pilot reads it.

Caution

**Same instance only.** Components work only inside the GitLab instance that hosts Preflight, so another instance needs a mirror. git.wayne.edu has no runner yet, so for now CI runs on the instance that has one. **A git.wayne.edu instance runner is strongly recommended.**

Note

**Every image is pinned by digest** (`name:tag@sha256:…`), so a repointed tag cannot quietly change what a pipeline runs. The `php-test` matrix is the one exception, tag-pinned on purpose so each job gets the newest PHP patch. Pins change only through a reviewed merge request.

```
$ docker buildx imagetools inspect <image>:<tag>
```

Preflight's own preflight

#### The checklist checks the checklist

`composer ci` lints every template and workflow for unsafe CI patterns before the fixture tests run.

- `privileged` `privileged: true`
- `dind-service` Docker-in-Docker services
- `docker-sock` references to `docker.sock`
- `kaniko-image` Kaniko images
- `unpinned-action` GitHub `uses:` not pinned to a 40-character SHA
- `image-no-tag` an image with no tag
- `image-latest` an image on `latest`
- `image-no-digest` a warning: tagged, but not pinned by digest

A known warning goes in `lint-allow.yml`, and every entry needs a `reason`, so someone has to write down why. On every pipeline, `contract/inputs.json` also holds each input's name, type and default, and each job's name, steady within a major version.

Wayne State app stack

### Departures

Preflight is one stop on the way to Citadel. Here is everyone else on the board.

- [WayneUI](https://wayneui.apps.wayne.edu/) The interface. Its a11y floor is the one Preflight's accessibility suite will aim at.
- [CREED](https://creed.apps.wayne.edu/) The written standards, and the policy every other part reads.
- [Pinstripe](https://pinstripe.apps.wayne.edu/) The coding standard behind the Pint, PHPStan and ESLint jobs.
- [PROCTOR](https://proctor.apps.wayne.edu/) One command that checks an app. First item on the checklist.
- Preflight Shared CI on every push. **You are here.**
- [Squire](https://squire.apps.wayne.edu/) Carries the cleared release to Citadel.
- [Rollcall](https://rollcall.apps.wayne.edu/) Every app answers "present". Skipped gates show up here.
- [Booster](https://booster.apps.wayne.edu/) Keeps an app's PHP current, so it stays on the test matrix.
- [HELMET](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/) Security headers and runtime hardening.
- [SESAME](https://sesame.apps.wayne.edu/) Sign-in for the app.
- [Drawbridge](https://drawbridge.apps.wayne.edu/) Signs people in through Entra ID before they reach a Citadel app.
- [ADVISOR](https://advisor.apps.wayne.edu/) Ask what applies to your app, and what to do next.
- [Sourdough](https://sourdough.apps.wayne.edu/) Starters you feed, with Preflight already in the pipeline.
- [WELD](https://weld.apps.wayne.edu/) A Laravel app with Inertia and Vue, with every part already installed.

All notable changes to PREFLIGHT are recorded here. Entries follow [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/); released versions are Git tags.

### Unreleased[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.html#unreleased)

- Added: a Composer cache on the proctor component, keyed on composer.lock (BEST_PRACTICES 4.8); new test tests/check-proctor-cache.
- Added: the docs site at `site/docs/`, built from `docs/` by Squire's shared docs builder (`bin/docs-site.php`), starting with the overview page. New composer scripts: `docs` builds it, `docs:check` fails when it is stale, and `ci` now runs the check.
- Docs: component pins in the README and site examples now point at 0.1.4.
- Changed: the front-page deploy layer pins HELMET ^0.3, PROCTOR ^0.4 and CREED ^0.1 (lock: HELMET 0.3.0, PROCTOR 0.4.0, CREED 0.1.6).
- Changed: the deploy layer sets minimum-stability to stable.
- Changed: phpstan config and memory_limit, pint config and sbom output now carry an input regex (relative paths and PHP sizes only); a value outside it stops the pipeline at creation. New test tests/check-path-input-regex.
- Added: a tag-triggered `release` job in the repository's own pipeline: pushing a protected tag creates the GitLab Release through the Releases API with curl, and the release notes carry the tag's commit SHA so consumers can pin it (BEST_PRACTICES 1.3, 1.6); new test tests/check-release-job.
- Added: a packageRule in `renovate/default.json` that restricts `quay.io/buildah/stable` to `-immutable` tags (regex versioning), so Renovate never moves a pin back to a mutable tag after Red Hat re-pushed one and garbage-collected the old digest; new test tests/check-renovate-buildah.
- Changed: the portability component's `buildah_image` default moves to the immutable tag `quay.io/buildah/stable:v1.43.5-immutable@sha256:7c2b605262748ace2c5c57c5550942d0adad57aec82ede3070927722306c0ffb`; Red Hat re-pushed the plain version tag and garbage-collected the old digest, so pipelines pinned to the mutable tag broke. New test tests/check-buildah-pin.

## The composer-audit component[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-composer-audit.html#the-composer-audit-component)

Fresh eyes on the manifest: this component runs `composer audit --locked` and fails the pipeline on advisories. This page shows how to add the `composer-audit` component to your app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`, then how to run it on a weekly schedule so the check keeps running after code is merged.

### Include the component[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-composer-audit.html#include-the-component)

Goal: your app's pipeline fails whenever a locked dependency has a known advisory. Add the include to your app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/composer-audit@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      working_dir: .
```

### Inputs[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-composer-audit.html#inputs)

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `composer-audit` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `composer:2@sha256:b6dcd72ca98fa19d0e5b8476de179859704891fad06dd9e0b96833d4c430a5fc` | Docker image for the job. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run composer audit in, relative to the project root. |

Note

The template adds regexes to two inputs: `job_name` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$` and `working_dir` must match `^(\.|[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._/-]*)$`.

### What the job does[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-composer-audit.html#what-the-job-does)

The `composer:2` image already ships Composer, so no install step is needed. The job is `interruptible: true` with a `timeout: 30 minutes`. Its script changes into `working_dir` and runs `composer audit --locked`. The command exits non-zero when it finds advisories, which fails the job.

Warning

The component carries no `allow_failure` input on purpose: a known advisory must fail the pipeline.

### Run it on a schedule[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-composer-audit.html#run-it-on-a-schedule)

New advisories are published after code is merged, so a green pipeline today can be stale tomorrow. Create a weekly pipeline schedule on the default branch: project settings, Build, Pipeline schedules. The component needs nothing extra; it carries no `rules:` block, so it runs in scheduled pipelines like any other. Creating the schedule is a project setting, not a file in the app's repo, and someone with Maintainer rights on the app must do it. It is the one Preflight check that books its own flight time.

### Related[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-composer-audit.html#related)

- [The proctor component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-proctor.html)
- [The php-test component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-php-test.html)

## The eslint component[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-eslint.html#the-eslint-component)

This page covers the `eslint` component: what the job does, how to include it, and every input it takes. Goal: the app's pipeline fails on any lint or format error, judged by the app's own config. Start with the include block, then check the inputs against your app. Preflight is named for the pre-flight check, and this component is the row that keeps the JavaScript airworthy.

Version 1 · Category: Testing/Validation · Tags: javascript,style,eslint,prettier

### What the job does[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-eslint.html#what-the-job-does)

The component runs the app's own [ESLint](https://eslint.org/) (and [Prettier](https://prettier.io/)) and fails the pipeline on lint or format errors. It does not install ESLint or Prettier itself: the app must require `@waynestate/pinstripe`, `eslint` and `prettier` as dev dependencies and ship an `eslint.config.js` (or point `eslint_args` at its own files).

The job, in order:

1. Moves into `working_dir` (default `.`).
2. Installs the app's dependencies with `npm ci --ignore-scripts --cache .npm-cache`.
3. Runs `npx --no-install eslint` with `eslint_args` (default `.`).
4. When `prettier` is `true` (the default), runs `npx --no-install prettier --check .`.

The job caches npm downloads in `.npm-cache/`, with the cache key based on `package-lock.json`. It is interruptible and times out after 15m.

### Include the component[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-eslint.html#include-the-component)

Add the include to the app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`, pinned to a full commit SHA with the tag in a trailing comment:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/eslint@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      eslint_args: .
```

### Inputs[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-eslint.html#inputs)

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `eslint` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `node:22.13-alpine@sha256:e2b39f7b64281324929257d0f8004fb6cb4bf0fdfb9aa8cedb235a766aec31da` | Docker image for the job. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run the commands in, relative to the project root. |
| `eslint_args` | string | `.` | Arguments passed to eslint. |
| `prettier` | boolean | `true` | Whether to also run `prettier --check`. |

### Verify[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-eslint.html#verify)

Push the change. The `eslint` job lands in the `test` stage by default, and a green job means ESLint and Prettier found nothing to fix.

Note

The `eslint` job has no `allow_failure` input: a lint or format error fails the pipeline.

### Related[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-eslint.html#related)

- [Quick start](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html): wire one component into an app and watch the pipeline run it.
- [Install](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html): the requirements, the include snippet, and how to verify.
- [The phpstan component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-phpstan.html): the static analysis check for the PHP side.

## The package-publish component[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-package-publish.html#the-package-publish-component)

This page covers the `package-publish` component: what the job does, how to include it, and every input it takes. Goal: tagging a release publishes the package to the GitLab group's built-in Composer registry, and a version that is already published never gets overwritten.

Version 1 · Category: Release/Publishing · Tags: composer,publish,release

### What the job does[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-package-publish.html#what-the-job-does)

The job publishes a semantic version tag to the GitLab group's built-in Composer registry. It runs only on tags, reads the registry first, and refuses a moved version: a version already published from this commit passes quietly, and a version published from a different commit fails the pipeline, because GitLab would otherwise overwrite it without a word. Once a version is on the manifest, it stays on the manifest: no go-arounds.

The job, in order:

1. Runs only when the pipeline is for a tag, so `$CI_COMMIT_TAG` is set.
2. Accepts only semantic versions, `1.2.3` or `v1.2.3` with an optional pre-release; any other tag fails the job.
3. Reads the package name from the `name` field of `composer.json` in the project root, the file the registry serves.
4. Reads the registry index with the read token. A `404` means the group has no published Composer packages yet, and the job goes straight to publishing.
5. Compares the commit recorded for the version, if any, with `$CI_COMMIT_SHA`: the same commit exits quietly, a different commit fails the job instead of overwriting the version.
6. Publishes the tag to the group's registry with the job token (`CI_JOB_TOKEN`) and reports the version as published.

The default image ships curl and PHP, which the job uses for the registry round trip. The job is interruptible and times out after 30 minutes.

Warning

Protect your release tags.

Note

The read token lives in a masked CI variable named by `read_token_variable` (default `PACKAGE_READ_TOKEN`) and needs the `read_package_registry` scope. Publishing itself uses the predefined `CI_JOB_TOKEN`.

### Include the component[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-package-publish.html#include-the-component)

Add the include to the app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`, pinned to a full commit SHA with the tag in a trailing comment, and set `group_id` to the numeric id of the GitLab group whose built-in Composer registry hosts the package:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/package-publish@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      group_id: "<your group id>"
```

### Inputs[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-package-publish.html#inputs)

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `deploy` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `package-publish` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `composer:2.10.3@sha256:b6dcd72ca98fa19d0e5b8476de179859704891fad06dd9e0b96833d4c430a5fc` | Docker image for the job. The default ships curl and PHP, which the job uses for the registry round trip. |
| `group_id` | string | none | Numeric id of the GitLab group whose built-in Composer registry hosts the package. Required. |
| `read_token_variable` | string | `PACKAGE_READ_TOKEN` | Name of the masked CI variable holding a token with the `read_package_registry` scope, used to read the registry before publishing. |

### Verify[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-package-publish.html#verify)

Define the masked CI variable the component reads, then push a semantic version tag. Expected: the `package-publish` job runs in the `deploy` stage, reads the registry, and ends with `Version <version> published.` Pushing the same tag from the same commit again exits quietly; the same version from a different commit fails the job.

### Related[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-package-publish.html#related)

- [Quick start](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html): wire one component into an app and watch the pipeline run it.
- [Install](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html): the requirements, the include snippet, and how to verify.
- [When the components run](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/when-components-run.html): the `workflow:rules` block that belongs in the app's own file.
- [Include a component twice](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/include-twice.html): the `job_name` input in action.
- [Reference](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html): every component, with its inputs and defaults.

## The php-test component[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-php-test.html#the-php-test-component)

Every engine gets its own check: this component runs your test command once per supported PHP version. This page shows how to add the `php-test` component to your app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`, how the matrix and the cache work, and how to trial the next PHP release. Next, add the [composer-audit component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-composer-audit.html).

### Include the component[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-php-test.html#include-the-component)

Goal: your app's test suite runs on each supported PHP version. The component runs the test command on each supported PHP version through `parallel:matrix`. Add the include to your app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      test_command: vendor/bin/phpunit
```

### Inputs[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-php-test.html#inputs)

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the jobs. |
| `job_name` | string | `php-test` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `php:${PHP_VERSION}-cli-trixie` | Docker image for the jobs. The default carries the literal `${PHP_VERSION}`, which GitLab expands in the image at job time. |
| `php_versions` | array | `["8.3", "8.4", "8.5"]` | PHP versions to test against. |
| `composer_version` | string | `2.10.3` | Composer version to install. |
| `test_command` | string | `vendor/bin/phpunit` | The test command to run. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run the command in, relative to the project root. |

Note

The template adds regexes to three inputs: `job_name` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$`, `composer_version` must match `^2\.\d+\.\d+$`, and `working_dir` must match `^(\.|[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._/-]*)$`.

### What the jobs do[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-php-test.html#what-the-jobs-do)

The array input feeds `parallel:matrix` directly, so one job is created per PHP version. `PHP_VERSION` becomes a CI/CD variable in each job, which the `image` input's default expands at job time. The default image is deliberately tag-pinned, so each job runs the newest patch release of its PHP version. Each job is `interruptible: true` with a `timeout: 30 minutes`, and its script:

1. Installs `unzip` and `git` with `apt-get`, because the `php:*-cli` images do not ship them (the images are Debian-based, so `apt` is used).
2. Copies the official Composer installer from `getcomposer.org` and verifies its SHA-384 against the signature fetched at runtime from `composer.github.io/installer.sig`. On a mismatch the check deletes the installer and exits 1. No `$` variables appear in the `php -r` code, so GitLab CI variable expansion cannot corrupt it.
3. Runs the installer quietly with `--install-dir=/usr/local/bin --filename=composer` and the pinned `composer_version`, so Composer lands on PATH, then removes `composer-setup.php`.
4. Changes into `working_dir` and runs `composer install --no-interaction --no-progress`.
5. Runs `test_command`.

### Caching[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-php-test.html#caching)

The jobs always cache Composer downloads in `.composer-cache/` so repeat runs do not re-download every package. The cache key depends on `composer.lock` and is prefixed with the PHP version, so a dependency change invalidates the cache and each PHP version gets its own cache:

```yaml
cache:
  key:
    files:
      - composer.lock
    prefix: php-${PHP_VERSION}
  paths:
    - .composer-cache/
  policy: pull-push
variables:
  COMPOSER_CACHE_DIR: "$CI_PROJECT_DIR/.composer-cache"
```

`COMPOSER_CACHE_DIR` points Composer at a path inside the project so GitLab can cache it.

### Try the next PHP release without breaking the pipeline[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-php-test.html#try-the-next-php-release-without-breaking-the-pipeline)

Include `php-test` a second time for the release that is not supported yet, name that job, and let it fail. The name is what lets your own `.gitlab-ci.yml` loosen only that job:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@<full commit SHA> # <tag>
    inputs:
      php_versions: ["8.6"]
      job_name: php-test-next
      # While 8.6 only has release candidate images, name the tag: php:${PHP_VERSION}-rc-cli-trixie
      # image: "php:${PHP_VERSION}-rc-cli-trixie"

php-test-next:
  allow_failure: true
```

A red `php-test-next` job is an early warning, not a stop. Drop the `allow_failure` and move the version into the main `php_versions` list once the release is supported (the supported versions follow `policy.json`).

### Related[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-php-test.html#related)

- [The proctor component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-proctor.html)
- [The composer-audit component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-composer-audit.html)

## The phpstan component[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-phpstan.html#the-phpstan-component)

This page shows how to add the `phpstan` component to an app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`: it runs the app's own [PHPStan](https://phpstan.org/) and fails the pipeline on static analysis errors, writing a GitLab Code Quality report. It finds the loose bolts before the flight does; check the requirements first, then add the include.

Version 1, category Testing/Validation, tags `php`, `static-analysis`, `phpstan`.

### Before you start[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-phpstan.html#before-you-start)

The component does not install PHPStan itself. The app must:

- Require `phpstan/phpstan` as a dev dependency.
- Ship a `phpstan.neon`, or point the `config` input at its own file.

### Include the component[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-phpstan.html#include-the-component)

Add the include to the app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`, pinned to a commit SHA with the tag in a trailing comment:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/phpstan@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      config: phpstan.neon
      memory_limit: 1G
```

A tag or branch can move; a SHA cannot.

### What the job does[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-phpstan.html#what-the-job-does)

The job lands in the `test` stage by default, is `interruptible: true`, and has a `timeout: 10m`. It runs three steps:

1. Move to the directory given by `working_dir` (default `.`).
2. Install the app's dependencies:
   ```sh
   composer install --no-interaction --no-progress --prefer-dist
   ```
3. Run PHPStan against the app's own config:
   ```sh
   vendor/bin/phpstan analyse --no-progress --error-format=gitlab --memory-limit=1G -c phpstan.neon > "$CI_PROJECT_DIR/phpstan-report.json"
   ```
   - `--memory-limit` takes the `memory_limit` input (default `1G`).
   - `-c` takes the `config` input (default `phpstan.neon`).
   - `--error-format=gitlab` writes the findings as a GitLab Code Quality report to `$CI_PROJECT_DIR/phpstan-report.json`.

### Report[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-phpstan.html#report)

The job publishes the report as a Code Quality report:

```yaml
artifacts:
  when: always
  reports:
    codequality: phpstan-report.json
```

### Inputs[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-phpstan.html#inputs)

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `phpstan` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `composer:2.10.3@sha256:b6dcd72ca98fa19d0e5b8476de179859704891fad06dd9e0b96833d4c430a5fc` | Docker image for the job. |
| `config` | string | `phpstan.neon` | Path to the app's PHPStan config file. It must be a relative path; GitLab refuses the pipeline at creation if it is not. |
| `memory_limit` | string | `1G` | Memory limit passed to PHPStan. A PHP size such as `1G`, `512M` or `-1`; GitLab refuses the pipeline at creation if it is not. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run PHPStan in, relative to the project root. |

`job_name` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$`, and `working_dir` must match `^(\.|[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._/-]*)$`.

Note

`config` must be a relative path, and `memory_limit` takes a PHP size such as `1G`, `512M` or `-1`. Each carries an input `regex`, so GitLab refuses the pipeline at creation when a value does not match.

### Verify[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-phpstan.html#verify)

Push the change. The components are ordinary jobs, so the `phpstan` job runs whenever the app's pipeline runs, in the `test` stage by default. A green job means no static analysis errors, and the Code Quality report carries the findings.

### Related[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-phpstan.html#related)

- [The pint component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-pint.html): the style check that pairs with it.
- [The proctor component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-proctor.html): another check that publishes a Code Quality report.
- [Include a component twice](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/include-twice.html): the `job_name` input when one project includes the same component more than once.
- [Reference](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html): every component, with its inputs and defaults.
