## The pint component[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-pint.html#the-pint-component)

This page shows how to add the `pint` component to an app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`: it runs the app's own [Laravel Pint](https://laravel.com/docs/12.x/pint) in test mode and fails the pipeline on style errors. It is the cockpit polish (every line tidied before takeoff); check the requirements first, then add the include.

Version 1, category Testing/Validation, tags `php`, `style`, `pint`.

### Before you start[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-pint.html#before-you-start)

The component does not install Pint itself. The app must:

- Require `laravel/pint` as a dev dependency.
- Ship a `pint.json`, or point the `config` input at its own file.

### Include the component[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-pint.html#include-the-component)

Add the include to the app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`, pinned to a commit SHA with the tag in a trailing comment:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/pint@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      config: pint.json
```

A tag or branch can move; a SHA cannot.

### What the job does[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-pint.html#what-the-job-does)

The job lands in the `test` stage by default, is `interruptible: true`, and has a `timeout: 10m`. It runs three steps:

1. Move to the directory given by `working_dir` (default `.`).
2. Install the app's dependencies:
   ```sh
   composer install --no-interaction --no-progress --prefer-dist
   ```
3. Run Pint in test mode against the app's own config:
   ```sh
   vendor/bin/pint --test --config=pint.json
   ```
   `--config` takes the `config` input (default `pint.json`). A style error fails the job, and with it the pipeline.

### Inputs[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-pint.html#inputs)

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `pint` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `composer:2.10.3@sha256:b6dcd72ca98fa19d0e5b8476de179859704891fad06dd9e0b96833d4c430a5fc` | Docker image for the job. |
| `config` | string | `pint.json` | Path to the app's Pint config file. It must be a relative path; GitLab refuses the pipeline at creation if it is not. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run Pint in, relative to the project root. |

`job_name` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$`, and `working_dir` must match `^(\.|[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._/-]*)$`.

Note

`config` must be a relative path. The input carries a `regex`, so GitLab refuses the pipeline at creation when a value does not match.

### Verify[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-pint.html#verify)

Push the change. The components are ordinary jobs, so the `pint` job runs whenever the app's pipeline runs, in the `test` stage by default. A green job means the app's code is clean under its own Pint config.

## The portability component[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-portability.html#the-portability-component)

The portability component proves your app image meets the twelve-factor boot contract: it builds the image, boots it the strict way, and validates it before anything else gets to run it. Like the real pre-flight, it is a list of checks you finish on the ground before you are cleared for takeoff. Add the include below to your app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`, then read what the two jobs check.

### What it checks[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-portability.html#what-it-checks)

Proves the app image meets the twelve-factor boot contract. It builds the image with Buildah (no Docker daemon, no elevated runner), boots it the strict way, and validates it with goss: the health path answers 200 for a foreign Host, the root filesystem and the app root are not writable, the app runs as the declared uid, and each declared writable path is writable. No takeoff without a clean pre-flight.

This is the twelve-factor boot check from ADR-0010: the app must start as a non-root user, write only to its declared paths, and answer its health path for any Host, not just its own.

### Add the include[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-portability.html#add-the-include)

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/portability@<full-commit-sha> # <tag, once one ships>
    inputs:
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
      context: .
      start_command: php -S 0.0.0.0:8080 -t public
```

Note

Portability ships in 0.1.4 and later (0.1.3 does not include it), so pin the `0.1.4` tag, or the full commit SHA of a commit at or after it.

Warning

The build job needs a runner that permits user namespaces (Buildah uses unshare for its storage); the run job needs only the project's container registry and an app image that carries curl, sha256sum and tar.

`start_command` is the one input with no default: it is app-specific, so you must set it.

### How the jobs work[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-portability.html#how-the-jobs-work)

The component is two jobs.

`portability-build` builds the image with Buildah, which needs no Docker daemon, and pushes it to the project's container registry. Buildah stores its layers with the vfs driver, which needs no special kernel support and runs in an ordinary container. Both jobs are interruptible and carry `timeout: 30 minutes`.

`portability-run` pulls that image, starts the app as an arbitrary uid, and validates it with goss. In order, the job:

1. Generates the goss file from the template and the inputs. The template is the same file the local checks use (`templates/portability/goss.yaml`); it is inlined in the component because a component only ships its `template.yml` to the including project. The `PORT`, `HEALTH_PATH`, `APP_ROOT` and `UID` placeholders are replaced with the inputs, and one command check per writable path is appended.
2. Downloads goss, pinned by version and checksum (v0.4.10, verified with `sha256sum -c`).
3. Starts the app in the background with `start_command`, then runs `goss validate` against the generated file, retrying the health check until the app answers or `boot_timeout` seconds expire.

goss runs as the app user (uid, gid 0), so the command checks see the same permissions the app has.

#### The goss checks[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-portability.html#the-goss-checks)

| Check | Command or request | What it asserts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Health path | `http://127.0.0.1:{{PORT}}{{HEALTH_PATH}}`, `method: GET`, request header `Host: portability-check.invalid` | The app answers 200 for a foreign Host, not just its own. |
| `root-not-writable` | `test ! -w /` | The app cannot write to the root of the filesystem. |
| `app-root-not-writable` | `test ! -w {{APP_ROOT}}` | The app cannot write to its own root directory. |
| `runs-as-uid` | `test "$(id -u)" = "{{UID}}"` | The app runs as the declared uid, not root. |
| One `writable-...` check per entry of `writable_paths` | `test -w <app_root>/<path>` | Each declared writable path is writable by the app user. |

Note

goss sends the method as written, so the health check uses upper case `GET`.

### Inputs[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-portability.html#inputs)

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the portability jobs. |
| `image` | string | `$CI_REGISTRY_IMAGE/portability:$CI_COMMIT_SHORT_SHA` | App image the portability-run job starts and validates. The default is what portability-build pushes; GitLab expands the CI variables at job time. |
| `buildah_image` | string | `quay.io/buildah/stable:v1.43.5-immutable@sha256:7c2b605262748ace2c5c57c5550942d0adad57aec82ede3070927722306c0ffb` | Buildah image for the portability-build job; it builds and pushes the app image. |
| `dockerfile` | string | `Dockerfile` | Dockerfile to build, relative to the context. |
| `context` | string | `.` | Build context, relative to the project root. |
| `app_root` | string | `/app` | Directory inside the image where the app lives. |
| `writable_paths` | array | `["storage", "bootstrap/cache"]` | Paths the app may write to, relative to app_root. Each must be writable by the app user. |
| `port` | number | `8080` | Port the app listens on inside the container. |
| `health_path` | string | `/up` | Path the app must answer 200 on for any Host. |
| `uid` | number | `100123` | Numeric uid the app runs as. The gid is always 0. |
| `start_command` | string | none | Command that starts the app inside the image. It is app-specific, so it is required and has no default. |
| `boot_timeout` | number | `60` | Seconds goss retries the health check while the app boots. |

The default is an immutable tag (`-immutable`) pinned by digest, because the plain version tag can be re-pushed and its old digest removed.

### Verify locally[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-portability.html#verify-locally)

The goss template is the same file the local checks use. `tests/check-portability.sh` (and its `.ps1` twin) do the placeholder replacement for the fixtures and build and boot the three fixtures under `tests/portability` the strict way; they exit 0 only when `good` passes and both `bad-*` fixtures fail. See [Local checks](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/local-checks.html) for the commands.

### Related[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-portability.html#related)

- [Include a component twice](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/include-twice.html): the `job_name` input, and why `portability` keeps its two fixed job names instead.
- [Same instance only](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/same-instance-only.html): components run only inside the GitLab instance that hosts this project.
- [When the components run](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/when-components-run.html): the `workflow:rules` block that belongs in the app's own file.
- [Reference](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html): every component, with its inputs and defaults.

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-proctor.html

## The proctor component[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-proctor.html#the-proctor-component)

A proctor keeps an eye on the exam hall; this one keeps an eye on your app. This page shows how to add the `proctor` component to your app's `.gitlab-ci.yml` and what the job does once it runs. Next, add the [php-test component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-php-test.html) so the test suite runs on every supported PHP version.

### Include the component[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-proctor.html#include-the-component)

Goal: your app's pipeline runs PROCTOR and publishes the result as a GitLab Code Quality report. Add the include to your app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/proctor@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      proctor_command: vendor/bin/proctor check --format=codequality
```

The job installs the app's dependencies with `composer install --no-plugins --no-scripts`, so the app's plugins and scripts never run inside the job.

Note

The install skips plugins and scripts on purpose: the job only inspects the app, so nothing in the app runs with the job's access.

### Inputs[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-proctor.html#inputs)

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `proctor` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `php:8.4-cli-trixie@sha256:9cf851bc2c1b37c3e59dfd677a3c3e56d485af5a47c93f629424bb039eafcb69` | Docker image for the job. |
| `composer_version` | string | `2.10.3` | Composer version to install. |
| `allow_failure` | boolean | `false` | Whether the job can fail without failing the pipeline. |
| `proctor_command` | string | `vendor/bin/proctor check --format=codequality` | The proctor command to run. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run the command in, relative to the project root. |

Note

The template adds regexes to three inputs: `job_name` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$`, `composer_version` must match `^2\.\d+\.\d+$`, and `working_dir` must match `^(\.|[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._/-]*)$`.

### What the job does[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-proctor.html#what-the-job-does)

The job is `interruptible: true` with a `timeout: 30 minutes`. Its script:

1. Installs `unzip` and `git` with `apt-get`, because the `php:8.4-cli-trixie` image does not ship them (the image is Debian-based, so `apt` is used).
2. Copies the official Composer installer from `getcomposer.org` and verifies its SHA-384 against the signature fetched at runtime from `composer.github.io/installer.sig`. On a mismatch the check deletes the installer and exits 1. No `$` variables appear in the `php -r` code, so GitLab CI variable expansion cannot corrupt it.
3. Runs the installer quietly with `--install-dir=/usr/local/bin --filename=composer` and the pinned `composer_version`, so Composer lands on PATH, then removes `composer-setup.php`.
4. Changes into `working_dir` and runs `composer install --no-interaction --no-progress --no-plugins --no-scripts`.
5. Runs `proctor_command` and redirects the output to `"$CI_PROJECT_DIR/gl-code-quality-report.json"`. A plain redirect (not `tee`) keeps proctor's exit code as the job result, and the report is written at the project root so the artifact path is the same for every `working_dir`, including `.`.

The job keeps Composer downloads in a cache under `.composer-cache/`, keyed on `composer.lock`, so repeat runs skip the download when the lock is unchanged.

The job publishes the report with `artifacts: when: always` as a GitLab Code Quality report (`reports: codequality: gl-code-quality-report.json`).

Tip

Set `allow_failure: true` if the job may fail without failing the pipeline; the default is `false`.

### Related[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-proctor.html#related)

- [The php-test component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-php-test.html)
- [The composer-audit component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-composer-audit.html)

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-renovate.html

## The renovate component[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-renovate.html#the-renovate-component)

This page covers the `renovate` component: what the job does, how to include it, and every input it takes. Goal: one scheduled job keeps image digests, GitHub action SHAs and package versions current across the group's repositories, and merges the updates whose pipeline is green. The component flies on autopilot; majors keep a human in the seat.

### What the job does[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-renovate.html#what-the-job-does)

The component runs [Renovate](https://docs.renovatebot.com/) as a scheduled or manual job that bumps image digests, GitHub action SHAs and package versions across the group's repositories, and merges the green ones itself. Bumps of `component:` include pins are covered by the preset and wait for review. Majors open a merge request and wait for a person. See [Renovate](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html) for what auto-merges and what waits.

Under the hood, the job:

- Runs only in scheduled pipelines (`$CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "schedule"`) and manual pipelines started from the web (`$CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "web"`).
- Points Renovate at the instance: `RENOVATE_PLATFORM` is `gitlab` and `RENOVATE_ENDPOINT` is `$CI_API_V4_URL`.
- Turns on autodiscovery (`RENOVATE_AUTODISCOVER: "true"`), limited to the `autodiscover_filter` glob, default `$CI_PROJECT_NAMESPACE/*`, relative to the runner project's namespace.
- Writes its `config.js` at job time. The `registryAliases` entry for the GitLab instance comes from the predefined `CI_SERVER_FQDN` variable: GitLab expands the key before the shell runs, and Node resolves the value when Renovate loads `config.js`. No hostname is stored in the template, so the public mirror stays clean.
- Passes `git_author` through as `RENOVATE_GIT_AUTHOR` and `dry_run` through as `RENOVATE_DRY_RUN`.
- Is interruptible and times out after 1 hour.

Warning

`RENOVATE_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_COM_TOKEN` are not set in the job's `variables:` on purpose. A self-reference such as `RENOVATE_TOKEN: $RENOVATE_TOKEN` arrives as literal text on GitLab 19.5 and shadows the masked project CI/CD variable, so the component leaves both tokens to the project and the masked values reach the job unchanged.

### Include the component[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-renovate.html#include-the-component)

Add the include to the runner project's `.gitlab-ci.yml`, pinned to a full commit SHA with the tag in a trailing comment, and set `git_author`:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/renovate@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      git_author: "Preflight Bot <preflight-bot@example.com>"
```

### Inputs[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-renovate.html#inputs)

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `job_name` | string | `renovate` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `renovate/renovate:44.192.2@sha256:37960a62ba1faa9079a7c4eead9b3f4470748a64ecd207e06c09fd8858673e17` | Docker image for the job. |
| `autodiscover_filter` | string | `$CI_PROJECT_NAMESPACE/*` | Glob limiting which projects Renovate discovers, relative to the runner project's namespace. |
| `dry_run` | string | `"null"` | Dry run mode: `null` (disabled), `lookup` or `full`. |
| `git_author` | string | none | Author of the commits and merge requests Renovate creates, in the form `Name <email>`. Required. |

### Verify[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-renovate.html#verify)

Start the job manually from the web, or wait for the schedule. Expected: the job bumps the versions it finds and merges the ones whose pipeline is green. To try it without changes, set `dry_run` to `lookup` or `full`; `null` (disabled) is the default.

### Related[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-renovate.html#related)

- [Renovate](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html): the shared preset, and what auto-merges, what waits and what waits for review.
- [Include a component twice](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/include-twice.html): the `job_name` input in action.
- [Quick start](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html): wire one component into an app and watch the pipeline run it.
- [Reference](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html): every component, with its inputs and defaults.

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-sbom.html

## The sbom component[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-sbom.html#the-sbom-component)

This page shows how to add the `sbom` component to an app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`: it generates a CycloneDX SBOM with `cyclonedx/cyclonedx-php-composer`, validates it, and publishes it as an artifact. The SBOM is the aircraft's parts manifest (nothing flies that is not on the list); start with the include, then read what the job does and which inputs it takes.

### Include the component[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-sbom.html#include-the-component)

Add the include to the app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`, pinned to a commit SHA with the tag in a trailing comment:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/sbom@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      output: sbom.cdx.json
```

A tag or branch can move; a SHA cannot.

### What the job does[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-sbom.html#what-the-job-does)

The job lands in the `test` stage by default, is `interruptible: true`, and has a `timeout: 30 minutes`. It runs four steps:

1. Install the app's dependencies:
   ```sh
   composer install --no-interaction --no-progress --prefer-dist
   ```
   The default image is a composer image, which already ships Composer, so no install step for Composer itself is needed.
2. Allow the CycloneDX plugin:
   ```sh
   composer global config --no-plugins allow-plugins.cyclonedx/cyclonedx-php-composer true
   ```
3. Install the plugin globally:
   ```sh
   composer global require cyclonedx/cyclonedx-php-composer:^6.2
   ```
   The plugin is installed globally, so the app's `composer.json` is never touched.
4. Generate the SBOM. `--validate` fails the job on an invalid SBOM:
   ```sh
   composer CycloneDX:make-sbom --output-format=JSON --output-reproducible --validate --omit=dev --output-file=sbom.cdx.json
   ```
   ```sh
   composer CycloneDX:make-sbom --output-format=JSON --output-reproducible --validate --output-file=sbom.cdx.json
   ```
   `--omit=dev` is present only when `omit_dev` is `true`; `--output-file` takes the `output` input (default `sbom.cdx.json`).

### Artifacts[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-sbom.html#artifacts)

The job publishes the SBOM file as an artifact:

```yaml
artifacts:
  paths:
    - sbom.cdx.json
  expire_in: 30 days
```

The path is the `output` input, and the artifact expires in 30 days.

### Inputs[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-sbom.html#inputs)

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `sbom` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `composer:2.10.3@sha256:b6dcd72ca98fa19d0e5b8476de179859704891fad06dd9e0b96833d4c430a5fc` | Docker image for the job. |
| `omit_dev` | boolean | `true` | Whether to omit dev dependencies from the SBOM. |
| `output` | string | `sbom.cdx.json` | Path of the SBOM file to publish, relative to the project root. It must be a relative path; GitLab refuses the pipeline at creation if it is not. |

`job_name` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$`.

Note

`output` must be a relative path. The input carries a `regex`, so GitLab refuses the pipeline at creation when a value does not match.

### Verify[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-sbom.html#verify)

Push the change. The components are ordinary jobs, so the `sbom` job runs whenever the app's pipeline runs, in the `test` stage by default. A green job means the SBOM was generated, validated, and published.

### Related[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-sbom.html#related)

- [The composer-audit component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-composer-audit.html): the companion dependency check.
- [Include a component twice](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/include-twice.html): the `job_name` input when one project includes the same component more than once.
- [When the components run](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/when-components-run.html): the `workflow:rules` block that belongs in the app's own file.
- [Reference](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html): every component, with its inputs and defaults.

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/github-mirrors.html

## GitHub mirrors[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/github-mirrors.html#github-mirrors)

Preflight's components fly inside one GitLab instance only, so this page shows how a package that is also mirrored to `github.com/waynestate` still gets the same checks: call Preflight's reusable GitHub Actions workflow from the mirror's own `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Start here, then read [Same instance only](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/same-instance-only.html) for why the components cannot cross instances.

### Why the mirror needs its own workflow[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/github-mirrors.html#why-the-mirror-needs-its-own-workflow)

Components work only inside one GitLab instance, so a package that is also mirrored to `github.com/waynestate` cannot include them there. For those mirrors, Preflight ships a reusable GitHub Actions workflow that runs the same checks: the package's `composer ci` script on each supported PHP version, plus a Composer audit.

### The workflow just calls `composer ci` [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/github-mirrors.html#the-workflow-just-calls-composer-ci)

Each package keeps its checks in a `ci` script in its `composer.json`; the workflow just calls `composer ci`, so the mirror runs whatever the package already runs on GitLab.

### Call the workflow from your package[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/github-mirrors.html#call-the-workflow-from-your-package)

The workflow lives at `.github/workflows/php-package.yml` in this repo. A mirrored package calls it from its own `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

```yaml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: ['**']
    tags: ['v*', '*.*.*']

jobs:
  ci:
    uses: waynestate/preflight/.github/workflows/php-package.yml@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
```

### Pin the include to a commit SHA[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/github-mirrors.html#pin-the-include-to-a-commit-sha)

This workflow ships in the `0.1.1` tag, so pin the full commit SHA of the release tag and keep the tag in a trailing comment. A tag or branch can move; a SHA cannot. PROCTOR's `preflight-pinned` check warns when an include is not pinned to a commit SHA. The Renovate preset (see the Renovate section) proposes the bumps, and they wait for review (the `needs-review` label).

### Workflow inputs[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/github-mirrors.html#workflow-inputs)

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `php-versions` | string (JSON array) | `'["8.3","8.4","8.5"]'` | PHP versions to test, lowest first. The audit job runs on the first entry. |
| `ci-command` | string | `composer ci` | The command to run in each PHP version job. |
| `working-directory` | string | `.` | Directory to run the command in, relative to the repository root. |

### Green on both sides[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/github-mirrors.html#green-on-both-sides)

The workflow is committed to this repo (and so to GitLab) but only runs on the GitHub mirror; GitLab ignores `.github/workflows`. A release tag is not done until it is green on both sides. Two cockpits, one checklist.

### Related[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/github-mirrors.html#related)

- [Same instance only](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/same-instance-only.html)
- [Renovate](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html)
- [Composer audit component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-composer-audit.html)

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/image-pins.html

## Updating image pins[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/image-pins.html#updating-image-pins)

This page covers the image pins Preflight's components run: why they are digests, how to look one up, and how to change one. Read the pinning rules, look up the new digest, and open a reviewed merge request. Like the aircraft preflight it is named after, the value shows up on the day it catches something.

### Why pins are digests[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/image-pins.html#why-pins-are-digests)

Every image the components run is pinned by digest (`name:tag@sha256:...`), so a repointed tag cannot quietly change what a pipeline executes. The tag stays in front of the digest so a diff still reads like a version bump.

Note

The php-test matrix is the one exception. Its PHP images are tag-pinned on purpose, so those jobs run on the newest PHP patch release; every other component image is digest-pinned.

### Look up the digest[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/image-pins.html#look-up-the-digest)

To look up the digest for an image:

```sh
docker buildx imagetools inspect <image>:<tag>
```

Use the top-level `Digest:` line (the multi-arch index digest), not a per-platform one. Without `buildx`, `docker manifest inspect -v <image>:<tag>` shows the same index digest.

### Change a pin[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/image-pins.html#change-a-pin)

Pins change only through a reviewed merge request.

### Related[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/image-pins.html#related)

- [Template lint](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/template-lint.html): the unsafe CI patterns `composer ci` scans for before the fixture tests.
- [Shared conventions](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/conventions.html): Composer vendor, license, PHP floor and JavaScript installs.

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/include-twice.html

## Include a component twice[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/include-twice.html#include-a-component-twice)

Goal: run the same component more than once in one project, for example in a monorepo with two apps, and keep the two jobs separate. Set the `job_name` input on each include, as shown below.

### Set `job_name` [#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/include-twice.html#set-job-name)

Every component except `portability` takes a `job_name` input, whose default is the job's usual name. Set it when one project includes the same component more than once, for example in a monorepo with two apps; without it the two jobs would share a name and merge into one.

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/pint@<full commit SHA> # <tag>
    inputs:
      working_dir: app
      job_name: pint-app
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/pint@<full commit SHA> # <tag>
    inputs:
      working_dir: admin
      job_name: pint-admin
```

Expected: the pipeline runs two separately named jobs, `pint-app` and `pint-admin`, instead of two jobs that merge into one.

Note

`job_name` ships in 0.1.4, so pin 0.1.4 or a SHA at or after that release. `portability` keeps its two fixed job names, because `portability-run` waits on `portability-build`.

### Another use: the next PHP release[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/include-twice.html#another-use-the-next-php-release)

Including a component twice is also how you try a PHP release before it is supported. Include `php-test` a second time for the release that is not supported yet, name that job, and let it fail. The name is what lets your own `.gitlab-ci.yml` loosen only that job:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@<full commit SHA> # <tag>
    inputs:
      php_versions: ["8.6"]
      job_name: php-test-next
      # While 8.6 only has release candidate images, name the tag: php:${PHP_VERSION}-rc-cli-trixie
      # image: "php:${PHP_VERSION}-rc-cli-trixie"

php-test-next:
  allow_failure: true
```

A red `php-test-next` job is an early warning, not a stop. Drop the `allow_failure` and move the version into the main `php_versions` list once the release is supported (the supported versions follow `policy.json`).

### Related[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/include-twice.html#related)

- [The php-test component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-php-test.html): inputs, caching, and the full next-release example.
- [The portability component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-portability.html): the one component without a `job_name` input.
- [When the components run](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/when-components-run.html): the `workflow:rules` block that belongs in the app's own file.
- [Reference](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html): every component, with its inputs and defaults.

## Strongly recommended: a git.wayne.edu instance runner[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/instance-runner.html#strongly-recommended-a-git-wayne-edu-instance-runner)

This page explains why a git.wayne.edu instance runner is strongly recommended and exactly what to ask for when you request one. Read it before you file the request, and carry the three asks below into the request itself.

### Why the recommendation exists[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/instance-runner.html#why-the-recommendation-exists)

Until git.wayne.edu has a runner, CI runs on the GitLab instance that has one, and Preflight and each app must live on or be mirrored to it. A git.wayne.edu instance runner is strongly recommended.

### What to ask for[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/instance-runner.html#what-to-ask-for)

Ask for:

- A non-privileged Docker executor (no privileged mode, no Docker socket mount).
- A fresh ephemeral environment for every job.
- No shell executor shared between projects.

Capacity and maintenance stay with ops.

Tip

A job that needs the host's Docker socket to take off has skipped its own preflight.

### Related[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/instance-runner.html#related)

- [Same instance only](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/same-instance-only.html)
- [When the components run](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/when-components-run.html)

## Keep the job token allowlist short[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/job-token-allowlist.html#keep-the-job-token-allowlist-short)

This page is for an app that installs private packages from GitLab's package registry. It sets out what belongs in the CI/CD job token allowlist, where the setting lives, and when to review it. Apply the rule once, then repeat the review whenever a dependency is dropped.

### What to list[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/job-token-allowlist.html#what-to-list)

An app that installs private packages from GitLab's package registry should list only the projects it really needs in its CI/CD job token allowlist (project settings, Settings, CI/CD, Job token permissions), use the fine-grained permissions where they fit, and review the list when a dependency is dropped.

Warning

A leaked job token acts with the triggering user's access.

### When to review[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/job-token-allowlist.html#when-to-review)

Review the list when a dependency is dropped, and drop any project the app no longer installs from it.

### What Preflight cannot do[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/job-token-allowlist.html#what-preflight-cannot-do)

This is a project setting, not a file Preflight can create or check. The setting is made in the app's GitLab project settings, so no file in the app's repository sets it for you.

### Related[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/job-token-allowlist.html#related)

- [What the components cannot force](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-components-cannot-force.html)
- [Install](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html)

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html

## Quick start[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#quick-start)

This quick start adds the `php-test` component to an app, the same way the front page shows it. Every other component installs the same way: one include, pinned to a commit SHA.

1. **Check the requirements.** Your GitLab must be 17.0 or newer (components are GA on the Free tier since GitLab 17.0), and the app must live on the same GitLab instance that hosts this project. Expected: both true, or the components cannot run here.
2. **Add the include** to the app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`:
   ```yaml
   include:
     - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
     inputs:
       test_command: vendor/bin/phpunit
   ```
   Expected: the file includes the component pinned to a full commit SHA, with the tag in a trailing comment. A tag or branch can move; a SHA cannot.
3. **Commit and push** the change:
   ```sh
   git push
   ```
   Expected: the next pipeline runs the `php-test` jobs, one per entry of `php_versions`, `8.3`, `8.4` and `8.5` by default, each in the `test` stage.
4. **Read the result.** Each job installs the app's dependencies, caches Composer downloads in `.composer-cache/`, and runs the test command. Expected: a green matrix, meaning the app passes on every supported PHP version.

### What you built[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#what-you-built)

Your app now runs the same PHP tests on each supported PHP version that every WSU app runs, from one pinned include. Add the remaining components the same way, one include each.

### Next steps[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html#next-steps)

- [Install](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html): requirements, the full include, and how to verify.
- [When the components run](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/when-components-run.html): the `workflow:rules` block that keeps the checks on merge requests and the default branch.
- [The php-test component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-php-test.html): inputs, caching, and trying the next PHP release without breaking the pipeline.
- [Reference](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html): every component, with its inputs and defaults.

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html

## Renovate: what merges and what waits[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html#renovate-what-merges-and-what-waits)

This page covers what Preflight's version automation auto-merges, what waits for a person, and how the private runner project is set up. For the component's inputs, go to [the `renovate` component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-renovate.html).

### How it works[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html#how-it-works)

Preflight owns the stack's version automation (ADR-0015): the shared preset `renovate/default.json` and the [`renovate` component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-renovate.html) that runs it. A private runner project includes the component on a schedule; Renovate discovers every repository in the filter, opens merge requests for outdated versions, and GitLab's native auto-merge takes in the ones whose pipeline is green.

Every stack repository carries a `renovate.json` that extends the shared preset, so the rules change in one place:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://docs.renovatebot.com/renovate-schema.json",
  "extends": ["local>enterprise-apps/preflight//renovate/default"]
}
```

### What auto-merges[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html#what-auto-merges)

Digest updates, pin and pinDigest updates, and patch and minor version bumps auto-merge when the pipeline is green. Lock file maintenance runs weekly and auto-merges the same way. Every merge request carries the `auto-deps` label.

The exception is Preflight's own pins: an update that touches the templates, the contract or this repository's own pipeline, a bump of a component include version, and a bump of the recorded Squire kit version, never auto-merge (see [What waits for review](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html#what-waits-for-review)).

### What waits[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html#what-waits)

Major version bumps never auto-merge. The merge request carries the `major` label and waits for a person.

### What waits for review[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html#what-waits-for-review)

Updates that change an image digest inside the templates, the contract, or this repository's own pipeline, bumps of a Preflight component version in an app's `component:` include, and bumps of the recorded Squire kit version (labeled `squire-kit`) carry the `needs-review` label and never auto-merge. They wait for a person because those pins are what every app pipeline runs: a changed digest here changes what every consuming pipeline executes, so it earns a human eye even when its own pipeline is green. The Squire kit version bump is refreshed by a person who runs `squire update` (with the right path for the repo), reviews the diff and commits it to the branch; the runner runs no commands, so the merge request carries no postUpgradeTasks.

### Why MySQL and HA-Proxy get digests only[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html#why-mysql-and-ha-proxy-get-digests-only)

The `mysql` and `haproxy` images mirror the versions Citadel actually runs, not the newest releases in the world. Bumping their tags would drift the apps away from production, so only digest updates are enabled for them: the same tag, the exact image. `citadel/php-apache` is disabled entirely, because Squire's own data owns that image.

### Pinned to immutable tags[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html#pinned-to-immutable-tags)

The `quay.io/buildah/stable` image (the `buildah_image` default of the portability component) is matched to `-immutable` tags only. Red Hat re-pushed v1.43.5 under the mutable tag and garbage-collected the old digest, which broke an image job, so DRAWBRIDGE and SQUIRE now pin the immutable form, `v1.43.5-immutable@sha256:...`. The preset carries a packageRule for `quay.io/buildah/stable` with a regex versioning that only matches `vX.Y.Z-immutable` tags, so Renovate proposes updates within the immutable tags and never moves a pin back to a mutable one. Digests stay pinned as before (`docker:pinDigests`).

### Set up (the user does this)[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html#set-up-the-user-does-this)

This repository ships the preset and the component, and creates nothing else. A person must set up:

- A private runner project that includes the `renovate` component on a schedule (see [The runner project](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html#the-runner-project)).
- The `RENOVATE_TOKEN` masked CI variable in that project, and optionally `GITHUB_COM_TOKEN`.
- A pipeline schedule on that project so the job runs regularly; weekly on Monday is a sensible default.

### The runner project[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html#the-runner-project)

Warning

The runner project must stay private. It holds `RENOVATE_TOKEN`, a token that can open and merge merge requests across the group, and this repository is mirrored to public GitHub. Use a group bot account for the token, not a person's: the bot outlives any one maintainer, and the commits keep one stable author.

| Variable | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `RENOVATE_TOKEN` | yes | Masked CI variable in the runner project; the job reads it straight from the project, the component does not map it. A project access token with Developer, or Maintainer where only Maintainers may merge. |
| `GITHUB_COM_TOKEN` | no | Masked CI variable in the runner project; the job reads it straight from the project, the component does not map it. Lookups against github.com do not hit anonymous rate limits. |

Warning

Do not add `RENOVATE_TOKEN: $RENOVATE_TOKEN` to your own `variables:`; that self-reference arrives as literal text.

The component writes its `config.js` at job time, so the `registryAliases` entry for the GitLab instance comes from the predefined `CI_SERVER_FQDN` variable. No hostname is stored in this repository.

### Related[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html#related)

- [The `renovate` component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-renovate.html)
- [GitHub mirrors](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/github-mirrors.html)
- [Image pins](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/image-pins.html)
- [Quick start](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html)

## Same instance only[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/same-instance-only.html#same-instance-only)

This page tells you where Preflight components can run, and what to do when your app is not on the right instance. Read it before you add an include if your app lives on a different GitLab than this project.

### The rule[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/same-instance-only.html#the-rule)

Components work only inside the GitLab instance that hosts this project.

Warning

Components cannot be used across instances except by mirroring.

Every include in this manual takes the form `component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/<name>@<full commit SHA>`. The path is built from `$CI_SERVER_FQDN`, the instance the pipeline runs on, so the component must be resolvable on that same instance.

### What that means for your app[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/same-instance-only.html#what-that-means-for-your-app)

- Your app must live on the same GitLab instance that hosts this project; if it does not, the components cannot run here.
- Until git.wayne.edu has a runner, CI runs on the GitLab instance that has one, and Preflight and each app must live on or be mirrored to it. See [Strongly recommended: a git.wayne.edu instance runner](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/instance-runner.html).
- A package that is also mirrored to `github.com/waynestate` cannot include the components there, because GitHub is not a GitLab instance at all. For those mirrors, Preflight ships a reusable GitHub Actions workflow that runs the same checks: the package's `composer ci` script on each supported PHP version, plus a Composer audit. See [GitHub mirrors](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/github-mirrors.html).

### Mirroring is the only exception[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/same-instance-only.html#mirroring-is-the-only-exception)

The one way to use the components on another GitLab instance is mirroring: mirror this project to that instance, so the components live there too. Everything else in this manual assumes the app and the components share an instance.

### Related[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/same-instance-only.html#related)

- [GitHub mirrors](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/github-mirrors.html): the reusable GitHub Actions workflow for packages mirrored to `github.com/waynestate`.
- [Strongly recommended: a git.wayne.edu instance runner](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/instance-runner.html): where CI runs until git.wayne.edu has a runner.
- [When the components run](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/when-components-run.html): the `workflow:rules` block that belongs in the app's own file.

---

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/template-lint.html

## Template lint[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/template-lint.html#template-lint)

This page lists the unsafe CI patterns the template lint catches and how to allowlist a known warning. Run `composer ci` to see the lint, which runs before the fixture tests.

### What it runs[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/template-lint.html#what-it-runs)

`composer ci` runs `bin/lint-templates` before the fixture tests. The lint scans `templates/**/*.yml` and `.github/workflows/*.yml` for unsafe CI patterns.

### Rules[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/template-lint.html#rules)

| Rule | Catches |
| --- | --- |
| `privileged` | `privileged: true` |
| `dind-service` | Docker-in-Docker services |
| `docker-sock` | references to `docker.sock` |
| `kaniko-image` | Kaniko images |
| `unpinned-action` | GitHub `uses:` entries that are not pinned to a 40-character SHA |
| `image-no-tag` | image references with no tag |
| `image-latest` | image references with `latest` |
| `image-no-digest` | a warning for a tagged image that is not pinned by digest |

The container-build rules (`privileged`, `dind-service`, `docker-sock` and `kaniko-image`) are explained in BEST_PRACTICES.md 4.17.

### Allowlist a known warning[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/template-lint.html#allowlist-a-known-warning)

Known warnings can be allowlisted in `lint-allow.yml`. Each entry needs `file`, `rule` and `reason`; the reason is required so an allowlist entry is a reviewed decision, not a silence. The preflight checklist checks the checklist.

### Related[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/template-lint.html#related)

- [Updating image pins](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/image-pins.html): why component images are digest-pinned and how to change a pin.
- [Shared conventions](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/conventions.html): Composer vendor, license, PHP floor and JavaScript installs.

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-components-cannot-force.html

## What the components cannot force[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-components-cannot-force.html#what-the-components-cannot-force)

An included component is a set of ordinary jobs. The app's own `.gitlab-ci.yml` is merged over them, so an app can override a job's keys, skip it with `rules`, or delete the `include:` line. Preflight makes the safe pipeline the easy one; it does not lock it. Rollcall is where skipped or weakened gates will show up. A preflight checklist only works if the pilot reads it. This page lists which jobs may be allowed to fail and the five project settings that make the gates harder to skip.

### Which jobs may be allowed to fail[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-components-cannot-force.html#which-jobs-may-be-allowed-to-fail)

Only `proctor` takes an `allow_failure` input (default `false`). A policy finding is a warning while an app adopts PROCTOR's rules, so the job may fail without failing the pipeline during adoption. `composer-audit` has no such input on purpose: a known advisory must fail the pipeline. The other jobs have no `allow_failure` input either.

No template adds a global key such as `default:`, `variables:`, `workflow:` or `stages:`. `tests/check-contract.sh` (and its `.ps1` twin) fails on any top-level key in a template that is not a job named in `contract/inputs.json`, so a global key fails `composer ci`.

### Protection checklist[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-components-cannot-force.html#protection-checklist)

A pilot signs each line of the checklist; the plane does not sign for you. Five project settings make the gates harder to skip, and every one of them works on GitLab Community Edition:

- **Protect the default branch** and require a merge request to change it. Every change to `.gitlab-ci.yml` then gets a reviewer. (Code owner approval needs Premium, so on Community Edition the reviewer is whoever merges.)
- **Protect the release tags.** Protect `*` or the release tag pattern so only maintainers can create or move a tag. A component ref is a tag, so whoever can move it controls every pipeline that pins it.
- **Set merge request approvals to at least one** for changes to the default branch. Approvals are available on every tier, but code owner rules within them need Premium, so on Community Edition the approval rests with whoever has merge rights: rely on the merger as the reviewer.
- **Set "Minimum role to use pipeline variables" to `no_one_allowed`** unless the project needs pipeline variables. The components take inputs, which are fixed and type checked for the whole run. Self-managed GitLab defaults this setting to `maintainer`.
- **Keep secrets away from fork merge requests.** A fork's merge request pipeline runs the fork's configuration. Review a fork's `.gitlab-ci.yml` before running its pipeline, and never give it protected variables.

Note

These are project settings Preflight cannot create or check, and a read-only token drift report was considered and left out on purpose: it would trade a token for a warning, and the checklist costs nothing to keep.

### Related[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-components-cannot-force.html#related)

- [When the components run](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/when-components-run.html)
- [The job token allowlist](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/job-token-allowlist.html)
- [GitHub mirrors](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/github-mirrors.html)
- [The `proctor` component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-proctor.html)

## When the components run[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/when-components-run.html#when-the-components-run)

The components are ordinary jobs, so they run whenever the app's pipeline runs. This page shows the `workflow:rules` block that runs them on every merge request and on pushes to the default branch, and why that block must live in the app's own file.

### The workflow:rules block[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/when-components-run.html#the-workflow-rules-block)

To run the components on every merge request and on pushes to the default branch, put a `workflow:rules` block in the app's own `.gitlab-ci.yml`:

```yaml
workflow:
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH

include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/proctor@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/composer-audit@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/sbom@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/pint@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/phpstan@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/eslint@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
```

Note

The `workflow:rules` block must live in the app's own file. A component cannot set the pipeline's `workflow:rules` for the project that includes it, so the `merge_request_event` rule goes in the app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`.

### Related[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/when-components-run.html#related)

- [Quick start](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html)

[![Preflight's front page: the headline Preflight, 'Every push is cleared for takeoff.', the include block for the php-test component, and the runway mark set in a heading-indicator instrument.](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/hero.jpg)](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/index.html)

## Preflight[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#preflight)

![php ^8.3](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/badges/php.svg) ![license MIT](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/badges/license.svg) ![gitlab ci components: 9](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/badges/components.svg)

**Every push is cleared for takeoff.**

Preflight is a set of GitLab CI/CD components that give every WSU app the same checks: PROCTOR, PHP tests on each supported version, Composer audit, an SBOM, Pint, PHPStan and ESLint. One include per component, pinned to a commit SHA, and the same checklist flies on every push.

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      test_command: vendor/bin/phpunit
```

### Pick your path[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/#pick-your-path)

- [Quick start](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html): wire one component into an app and watch the pipeline run it.
- [Install](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html): the requirements, the include snippet, and how to verify the pipeline picked the component up.
- [Reference](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html): every component, with its include example, inputs and defaults.

Preflight 0.1.4; GitLab components are GA on the Free tier since GitLab 17.0; MIT licensed.

Agents: fetch [https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/llms.txt) for a machine-readable index of this manual.

---

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html

## Install[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#install)

Preflight installs as an `include:` in the app's own `.gitlab-ci.yml`, one line per component, pinned to a commit SHA with the tag in a trailing comment. A tag or branch can move; a SHA cannot.

### Requirements[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#requirements)

- GitLab 17.0 or newer. Components are GA on the Free tier since GitLab 17.0.
- Same instance only. Components work only within the same GitLab instance that hosts this project; they cannot be used across instances except by mirroring.

### Install[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#install-1)

Add the include to the app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/proctor@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/composer-audit@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/sbom@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/pint@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/phpstan@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/eslint@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
```

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      test_command: vendor/bin/phpunit
```

### Verify[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#verify)

Push the change. The components are ordinary jobs, so they run whenever the app's pipeline runs, and each one lands in the `test` stage by default. Expected result: the pipeline shows the component's job, and for `php-test` that is one job per entry of `php_versions`, `8.3`, `8.4` and `8.5` by default. A green job means the check passed.

### Next steps[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.html#next-steps)

- [Quick start](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.html): the same install as numbered steps with expected results.
- [When the components run](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/when-components-run.html): the `workflow:rules` block that belongs in the app's own file.
- [The php-test component](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/component-php-test.html): inputs, caching, and trying the next PHP release.
- [Reference](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html): every component, with its inputs and defaults.
