Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html

## Components[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#components)

Every GitLab CI component Preflight ships, with its include example, its inputs and their defaults, and the jobs and timeouts each template defines. Add one include to your app's `.gitlab-ci.yml`, then follow the per-component guide for setup. Like a real pre-flight check, the point is to find the fault on the ground, where it is cheap to fix.

Note

Components are GA on the Free tier since GitLab 17.0. They work only within the same GitLab instance that hosts this project.

![Preflight's before-takeoff checklist card. 1 PROCTOR, checked; 2 PHP tests, 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5 pass; 3 Composer audit, no advisories; 4 SBOM, validated; 5 Pint, clean; 6 PHPStan, no errors; 7 ESLint and Prettier, clean; 8 clearance, cleared for takeoff. Beside it the annunciator panel lights a green lamp per check, with a11y, contract and freshness marked coming soon, and lists the seven checks, all in the 0.1.4 tag.](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/readme/checklist.svg)

The checklist, item by item, with each item's job and timeout read from `templates/`:

| # | Item | Job | Timeout |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | PROCTOR | `proctor` | 30 minutes |
| 2 | PHP tests, 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5 | `php-test`, one job per version | 30 minutes |
| 3 | Composer audit | `composer-audit` | 30 minutes |
| 4 | SBOM | `sbom` | 30 minutes |
| 5 | Pint | `pint` | 10m |
| 6 | PHPStan | `phpstan` | 10m |
| 7 | ESLint and Prettier | `eslint` | 15m |

Every job the templates define is `interruptible: true`. Every component except `portability` takes a `job_name` input whose default is the job's usual name; set it when one project includes the same component more than once. `portability` keeps its two fixed job names, because `portability-run` waits on `portability-build`.

### proctor[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#proctor)

Runs `vendor/bin/proctor check --format=codequality` and publishes the result as a GitLab Code Quality report. The job installs the app's dependencies with `composer install --no-plugins --no-scripts`, so the app's plugins and scripts never run inside the job.

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/proctor@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      proctor_command: vendor/bin/proctor check --format=codequality
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `proctor` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `php:8.4-cli-trixie@sha256:9cf851bc2c1b37c3e59dfd677a3c3e56d485af5a47c93f629424bb039eafcb69` | Docker image for the job. |
| `composer_version` | string | `2.10.3` | Composer version to install. |
| `allow_failure` | boolean | `false` | Whether the job can fail without failing the pipeline. |
| `proctor_command` | string | `vendor/bin/proctor check --format=codequality` | The proctor command to run. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run the command in, relative to the project root. |

From `templates/proctor/template.yml`: the single job (named by `job_name`) runs in the `test` stage by default, is `interruptible: true`, and has a timeout of 30 minutes. It installs Composer with the official getcomposer.org installer, verifies the installer's SHA-384 against composer.github.io/installer.sig, and pins the installed version to `composer_version`. It then runs `composer install --no-interaction --no-progress --no-plugins --no-scripts`, so the app's plugins and scripts never run with the job's access. The command's output goes through a plain redirect (not `tee`) to `gl-code-quality-report.json` at the project root, which keeps PROCTOR's exit code as the job result and gives the artifact the same path for every `working_dir`, including `.`. The report is published as a Code Quality report with `when: always`.

### php-test[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#php-test)

Runs the test command on each supported PHP version through `parallel:matrix`.

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      test_command: vendor/bin/phpunit
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the jobs. |
| `job_name` | string | `php-test` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `php:${PHP_VERSION}-cli-trixie` | Docker image for the jobs. The default carries the literal `${PHP_VERSION}`, which GitLab expands in the image at job time. |
| `php_versions` | array | `["8.3", "8.4", "8.5"]` | PHP versions to test against. |
| `composer_version` | string | `2.10.3` | Composer version to install. |
| `test_command` | string | `vendor/bin/phpunit` | The test command to run. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run the command in, relative to the project root. |

From `templates/php-test/template.yml`: one job is created per entry in `php_versions` through `parallel:matrix`; `PHP_VERSION` becomes a CI/CD variable in each job, which the image input's default expands, and each job runs the newest patch release of its version. The default image is deliberately tag-pinned (the template points at the README section Updating image pins). Each job installs Composer the same way as proctor, runs `composer install --no-interaction --no-progress`, and then the test command. The jobs are `interruptible: true` with a timeout of 30 minutes.

#### Caching[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#caching)

The jobs always cache Composer downloads in `.composer-cache/` so repeat runs do not re-download every package. The cache key depends on `composer.lock` and is prefixed with the PHP version, so a dependency change invalidates the cache and each PHP version gets its own cache. The template sets `COMPOSER_CACHE_DIR` to `$CI_PROJECT_DIR/.composer-cache`, keys the cache on `composer.lock` with the prefix `php-${PHP_VERSION}`, caches the path `.composer-cache/`, and uses the policy `pull-push`.

#### Try the next PHP release without breaking the pipeline[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#try-the-next-php-release-without-breaking-the-pipeline)

Include `php-test` a second time for the release that is not supported yet, name that job, and let it fail. The name is what lets your own `.gitlab-ci.yml` loosen only that job:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/php-test@<full commit SHA> # <tag>
    inputs:
      php_versions: ["8.6"]
      job_name: php-test-next
      # While 8.6 only has release candidate images, name the tag: php:${PHP_VERSION}-rc-cli-trixie
      # image: "php:${PHP_VERSION}-rc-cli-trixie"

php-test-next:
  allow_failure: true
```

A red `php-test-next` job is an early warning, not a stop. Drop the `allow_failure` and move the version into the main `php_versions` list once the release is supported (the supported versions follow `policy.json`).

### composer-audit[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#composer-audit)

Runs `composer audit --locked` and fails on advisories.

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/composer-audit@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      working_dir: .
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `composer-audit` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `composer:2@sha256:b6dcd72ca98fa19d0e5b8476de179859704891fad06dd9e0b96833d4c430a5fc` | Docker image for the job. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run composer audit in, relative to the project root. |

From `templates/composer-audit/template.yml`: the `composer:2` image already ships Composer, so there is no install step. The job runs `composer audit --locked`, which exits non-zero when it finds advisories, and fails the job. There is no `allow_failure` input: advisories must fail. The job is `interruptible: true` with a timeout of 30 minutes.

#### Run it on a schedule[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#run-it-on-a-schedule)

New advisories are published after code is merged, so a green pipeline today can be stale tomorrow. Create a weekly pipeline schedule on the default branch: project settings, Build, Pipeline schedules. The component needs nothing extra; it carries no `rules:` block, so it runs in scheduled pipelines like any other. Creating the schedule is a project setting, not a file in the app's repo, and someone with Maintainer rights on the app must do it. It is the one preflight check that books its own flight time.

### sbom[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#sbom)

Generates a CycloneDX SBOM with `cyclonedx/cyclonedx-php-composer`, validates it, and publishes it as an artifact. The plugin is installed globally, so the app's `composer.json` is never touched.

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/sbom@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      output: sbom.cdx.json
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `sbom` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `composer:2.10.3@sha256:b6dcd72ca98fa19d0e5b8476de179859704891fad06dd9e0b96833d4c430a5fc` | Docker image for the job. |
| `omit_dev` | boolean | `true` | Whether to omit dev dependencies from the SBOM. |
| `output` | string | `sbom.cdx.json` | Path of the SBOM file to publish, relative to the project root. |

From `templates/sbom/template.yml`: the job runs `composer install --no-interaction --no-progress --prefer-dist`, allows the plugin globally with `composer global config --no-plugins allow-plugins.cyclonedx/cyclonedx-php-composer true`, installs `cyclonedx/cyclonedx-php-composer:^6.2` globally, and then runs `composer CycloneDX:make-sbom --output-format=JSON --output-reproducible --validate` with `--omit=dev` added while `omit_dev` is true, writing to the `output` path. The `--validate` flag fails the job on an invalid SBOM. The SBOM file is published as an artifact with `expire_in: 30 days`. The job is `interruptible: true` with a timeout of 30 minutes.

### pint[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#pint)

Version 1 · Category: Testing/Validation · Tags: php,style,pint

Runs the app's own [Laravel Pint](https://laravel.com/docs/12.x/pint) in test mode and fails the pipeline on style errors. The app must require `laravel/pint` as a dev dependency and ship a `pint.json` (or point `config` at its own file).

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/pint@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      config: pint.json
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `pint` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `composer:2.10.3@sha256:b6dcd72ca98fa19d0e5b8476de179859704891fad06dd9e0b96833d4c430a5fc` | Docker image for the job. |
| `config` | string | `pint.json` | Path to the app's Pint config file. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run Pint in, relative to the project root. |

From `templates/pint/template.yml`: the component does not install Pint itself; it runs `composer install --no-interaction --no-progress --prefer-dist` and then the app's own Pint in test mode against the `config` file. The job is `interruptible: true` with a timeout of 10m.

### phpstan[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#phpstan)

Version 1 · Category: Testing/Validation · Tags: php,static-analysis,phpstan

Runs the app's own [PHPStan](https://phpstan.org/) and fails the pipeline on static analysis errors, writing a GitLab Code Quality report. The app must require `phpstan/phpstan` as a dev dependency and ship a `phpstan.neon` (or point `config` at its own file).

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/phpstan@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      config: phpstan.neon
      memory_limit: 1G
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `phpstan` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `composer:2.10.3@sha256:b6dcd72ca98fa19d0e5b8476de179859704891fad06dd9e0b96833d4c430a5fc` | Docker image for the job. |
| `config` | string | `phpstan.neon` | Path to the app's PHPStan config file. |
| `memory_limit` | string | `1G` | Memory limit passed to PHPStan. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run PHPStan in, relative to the project root. |

From `templates/phpstan/template.yml`: the component does not install PHPStan itself; it runs `composer install --no-interaction --no-progress --prefer-dist` and then the app's own PHPStan with `--no-progress --error-format=gitlab`, the `memory_limit` value and the `config` file, redirecting the output to `$CI_PROJECT_DIR/phpstan-report.json`. The report is published as a Code Quality report with `when: always`. The job is `interruptible: true` with a timeout of 10m.

### eslint[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#eslint)

Version 1 · Category: Testing/Validation · Tags: javascript,style,eslint,prettier

Runs the app's own [ESLint](https://eslint.org/) (and [Prettier](https://prettier.io/)) and fails the pipeline on lint or format errors. The app must require `@waynestate/pinstripe`, `eslint` and `prettier` as dev dependencies and ship an `eslint.config.js` (or point `eslint_args` at its own files).

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/eslint@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      eslint_args: .
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `eslint` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `node:22.13-alpine@sha256:e2b39f7b64281324929257d0f8004fb6cb4bf0fdfb9aa8cedb235a766aec31da` | Docker image for the job. |
| `working_dir` | string | `.` | Directory to run the commands in, relative to the project root. |
| `eslint_args` | string | `.` | Arguments passed to eslint. |
| `prettier` | boolean | `true` | Whether to also run `prettier --check`. |

From `templates/eslint/template.yml`: the component does not install ESLint or Prettier itself; it runs `npm ci --ignore-scripts --cache .npm-cache` (the cache is keyed on `package-lock.json` and stores `.npm-cache/`), then `npx --no-install eslint` with the `eslint_args` value, and, while `prettier` is true, `npx --no-install prettier --check .`. The job is `interruptible: true` with a timeout of 15m.

### package-publish[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#package-publish)

Version 1 · Category: Release/Publishing · Tags: composer,publish,release

Publishes a semantic version tag to the GitLab group's built-in Composer registry. The job runs only on tags, reads the registry first, and refuses a moved version: a version already published from this commit passes quietly, and a version published from a different commit fails the pipeline, because GitLab would otherwise overwrite it without a word. The default image ships curl and PHP, which the job uses for the registry round trip.

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/package-publish@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      group_id: "<your group id>"
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `deploy` | Pipeline stage for the job. |
| `job_name` | string | `package-publish` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `composer:2.10.3@sha256:b6dcd72ca98fa19d0e5b8476de179859704891fad06dd9e0b96833d4c430a5fc` | Docker image for the job. The default ships curl and PHP, which the job uses for the registry round trip. |
| `group_id` | string | none | Numeric id of the GitLab group whose built-in Composer registry hosts the package. Required. |
| `read_token_variable` | string | `PACKAGE_READ_TOKEN` | Name of the masked CI variable holding a token with the `read_package_registry` scope, used to read the registry before publishing. |

Warning

Protect your release tags.

From `templates/package-publish/template.yml`: the job runs only when `$CI_COMMIT_TAG` is set. The tag must be a semantic version, `1.2.3` or `v1.2.3` with an optional pre-release, or the job fails. The package name comes from `composer.json`, the file the registry serves. The job reads the masked CI variable named by `read_token_variable`, checks that `group_id` is numeric, reads the group's Composer registry index with the token, and follows the package metadata to the version already on the manifest. A version already published at this commit passes quietly (exit 0); a version published at a different commit fails (exit 1). Publishing posts the tag to the project's Composer packages endpoint with the job token. The job is `interruptible: true` with a timeout of 30 minutes.

### renovate[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#renovate)

Runs [Renovate](https://docs.renovatebot.com/) as a scheduled or manual job that bumps image digests, GitHub action SHAs and package versions across the group's repositories, and merges the green ones itself. Bumps of `component:` include pins are covered by the preset and wait for review. Majors open a merge request and wait for a person. See [Renovate](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html) for what auto-merges and what waits.

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/renovate@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
    inputs:
      git_author: "Preflight Bot <preflight-bot@example.com>"
```

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `job_name` | string | `renovate` | Name of the job. Set it when you include this component more than once. |
| `image` | string | `renovate/renovate:44.192.2@sha256:37960a62ba1faa9079a7c4eead9b3f4470748a64ecd207e06c09fd8858673e17` | Docker image for the job. |
| `autodiscover_filter` | string | `$CI_PROJECT_NAMESPACE/*` | Glob limiting which projects Renovate discovers, relative to the runner project's namespace. |
| `dry_run` | string | `"null"` | Dry run mode: `null` (disabled), `lookup` or `full`. |
| `git_author` | string | none | Author of the commits and merge requests Renovate creates, in the form `Name <email>`. Required. |

From `templates/renovate/template.yml`: the job has no `stage` input and sets no stage. It runs only on scheduled and manual pipelines (`$CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "schedule"` or `"web"`). It writes its `config.js` at job time, so the `registryAliases` entry for the GitLab instance comes from the predefined `CI_SERVER_FQDN` variable; no hostname is stored in the repository, so the public mirror stays clean. It does not set `RENOVATE_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_COM_TOKEN` in the job `variables:` on purpose: a self-reference such as `X: $X` arrives as literal text on GitLab 19.5 and would shadow the masked project CI/CD variables, so the job reads both tokens straight from the project. The job is `interruptible: true` with a timeout of 1 hour.

### portability[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html#portability)

Proves the app image meets the twelve-factor boot contract. It builds the image with Buildah (no Docker daemon, no elevated runner), boots it the strict way, and validates it with goss: the health path answers 200 for a foreign Host, the root filesystem and the app root are not writable, the app runs as the declared uid, and each declared writable path is writable. No takeoff without a clean pre-flight.

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/portability@<full-commit-sha> # <tag, once one ships>
    inputs:
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
      context: .
      start_command: php -S 0.0.0.0:8080 -t public
```

Portability ships in 0.1.4 and later (0.1.3 does not include it), so pin the `0.1.4` tag, or the full commit SHA of a commit at or after it. The build job needs a runner that permits user namespaces (Buildah uses unshare for its storage); the run job needs only the project's container registry and an app image that carries curl, sha256sum and tar.

| Input | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stage` | string | `test` | Pipeline stage for the portability jobs. |
| `image` | string | `$CI_REGISTRY_IMAGE/portability:$CI_COMMIT_SHORT_SHA` | App image the portability-run job starts and validates. The default is what portability-build pushes; GitLab expands the CI variables at job time. |
| `buildah_image` | string | `quay.io/buildah/stable:v1.43.5-immutable@sha256:7c2b605262748ace2c5c57c5550942d0adad57aec82ede3070927722306c0ffb` | Buildah image for the portability-build job; it builds and pushes the app image. |
| `dockerfile` | string | `Dockerfile` | Dockerfile to build, relative to the context. |
| `context` | string | `.` | Build context, relative to the project root. |
| `app_root` | string | `/app` | Directory inside the image where the app lives. |
| `writable_paths` | array | `["storage", "bootstrap/cache"]` | Paths the app may write to, relative to app_root. Each must be writable by the app user. |
| `port` | number | `8080` | Port the app listens on inside the container. |
| `health_path` | string | `/up` | Path the app must answer 200 on for any Host. |
| `uid` | number | `100123` | Numeric uid the app runs as. The gid is always 0. |
| `start_command` | string | none | Command that starts the app inside the image. It is app-specific, so it is required and has no default. |
| `boot_timeout` | number | `60` | Seconds goss retries the health check while the app boots. |

The default is an immutable tag (`-immutable`) pinned by digest, because the plain version tag can be re-pushed and its old digest removed.

From `templates/portability/template.yml`: the component defines two jobs with fixed names. `portability-build` runs in the `buildah_image`, sets `STORAGE_DRIVER: vfs` (the vfs driver needs no special kernel support and runs in an ordinary container), builds the image with `buildah bud`, logs in to the project's container registry, and pushes `$CI_REGISTRY_IMAGE/portability:$CI_COMMIT_SHORT_SHA`. `portability-run` needs `portability-build`, generates a goss file from the inputs (the goss template is inlined in the job, because a component only ships its `template.yml` to the including project), downloads goss pinned by version and checksum, starts the app with `start_command`, and runs `goss validate` with `--retry-timeout` set to `boot_timeout` seconds. goss runs as the app user (the declared uid, gid 0), so its command checks see the same permissions the app has. Both jobs are `interruptible: true` with a timeout of 30 minutes.

## Shared conventions[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/conventions.html#shared-conventions)

This page lists the conventions the stack shares: Composer vendor, license, PHP floor and JavaScript installs. Check a package against the table when you set one up or review one, so every project starts from the same baseline.

### Conventions[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/conventions.html#conventions)

| Convention | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Composer vendor | `waynestate/` |
| License | MIT |
| PHP floor | `^8.3` |

Preflight itself ships these values in its `composer.json`: `waynestate/preflight` under the MIT license, requiring `php: ^8.3`.

### JavaScript installs[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/conventions.html#javascript-installs)

JavaScript components install with `npm ci --ignore-scripts`. The job carries no token beyond `CI_JOB_TOKEN` (BEST_PRACTICES.md 4.12).

### Related[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/conventions.html#related)

- [Updating image pins](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/image-pins.html): why component images are digest-pinned and how to change a pin.
- [Template lint](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/template-lint.html): the unsafe CI patterns `composer ci` scans for before the fixture tests.

## Local checks[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/local-checks.html#local-checks)

How maintainers build, test and release this project with Docker, and the Composer scripts behind the gate. The pre-flight checklist, run from your own desk: run the same gate CI runs before you push anything.

Note

Maintainers: how to build, test and release this project, and where its data comes from, is in [MAINTAINING.md](https://nougat.snu.gs/enterprise-apps/preflight/-/blob/main/MAINTAINING.md) on the canonical repository.

### The full gate[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/local-checks.html#the-full-gate)

Run the template lint and the fixture tests with Docker:

```sh
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd):/app" -w /app composer:2 composer install
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd):/app" -w /app composer:2 composer ci
```

```powershell
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2 composer install
docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" -w /app composer:2 composer ci
```

In PowerShell, use `${PWD}` instead of `$(pwd)`. `composer ci` is the whole gate: it runs the template lint, the fixture tests, Pint, PHPStan, the agent-ready file check and the docs site check, in that order.

### Composer scripts[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/local-checks.html#composer-scripts)

The scripts from `composer.json`:

```json
{
    "ci": [
        "php bin/lint-templates",
        "php bin/lint-templates --test",
        "@lint",
        "@analyse",
        "@site:agent-ready-check",
        "@docs:check"
    ],
    "lint": "pint --test",
    "fix": "pint",
    "analyse": "phpstan analyse --memory-limit=1G",
    "site:agent-ready": "php bin/agent-ready.php",
    "site:agent-ready-check": "php bin/agent-ready.php --check",
    "docs": "php bin/docs-site.php",
    "docs:check": "php bin/docs-site.php --check"
}
```

| Script | Runs | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ci` | the array above | The full CI gate: template lint, fixture tests, Pint, PHPStan, agent-ready files, docs site. |
| `lint` | `pint --test` | Run Pint in test mode; fails on style errors without changing files. |
| `fix` | `pint` | Run Pint and rewrite the files it finds. |
| `analyse` | `phpstan analyse --memory-limit=1G` | Run PHPStan with a 1G memory limit. |
| `site:agent-ready` | `php bin/agent-ready.php` | Rewrite the Markdown twins, llms.txt, llms-full.txt, robots.txt and sitemap.xml in `site/` (Squire's agent-ready kit). |
| `site:agent-ready-check` | `php bin/agent-ready.php --check` | Fail when the agent-ready files are stale, a page lacks its Markdown link, a prompt drifts from the docs, or the kit was edited here. |
| `docs` | `php bin/docs-site.php` | Build the docs site from `docs/` into `site/docs/` (Squire's docs builder): render the pages, fill the generated command and environment reference, and stamp the current version. |
| `docs:check` | `php bin/docs-site.php --check` | Fail when the built docs site is stale or the generated command or environment reference has drifted from the CLI or source. |

### The PHP fixture app[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/local-checks.html#the-php-fixture-app)

Run the PHP fixture app separately:

```sh
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)/tests/fixture-app:/app" -w /app composer:2 composer install
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)/tests/fixture-app:/app" -w /app php:8.4-cli vendor/bin/phpunit
```

### The portability fixtures[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/local-checks.html#the-portability-fixtures)

Run the portability fixtures with Docker; they build and boot the three fixtures under `tests/portability` the strict way and exit 0 only when `good` passes and both `bad-*` fixtures fail:

```sh
sh tests/check-portability.sh
```

```powershell
pwsh -File tests/check-portability.ps1
```

### Proof[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/local-checks.html#proof)

Proof runs against real Wayne State applications are on a private site, [proof.apps.wayne.edu/preflight](https://proof.apps.wayne.edu/preflight/), behind a Wayne State employee sign-in.

### Docs[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/local-checks.html#docs)

The full documentation lives at [preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/) on the project site, built from `docs/` by Squire's docs builder. It starts with the overview page; the rest of the manual follows as the pages are written.

- `composer docs` rebuilds `site/docs/` from `docs/`; run it after editing a page.
- `composer docs:check` fails when the built site is stale; `composer ci` runs it.

The pages are committed because the deploy server serves `site/` without building. Every page links back to its Markdown, and the footer stamps the version the docs describe. Cleared for takeoff: the flight manual flies with the aircraft.

## Troubleshooting[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#troubleshooting)

What to do when a Preflight job fails or a gate behaves unexpectedly. Each entry names the cause, the fix, and how to check it. Most failures are a pin that moved or a setting that is missing. The checklist catches the rest.

Tip

Start with the job log. The message usually names the input that is wrong, and every input is listed on the [Components](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html) page.

### The pipeline[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-pipeline)

#### The include fails on another GitLab instance[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-include-fails-on-another-gitlab-instance)

Components work only inside the GitLab instance that hosts this project, and they cannot be used across instances except by mirroring.

- **Cause:** the app lives on a different instance than the one that hosts Preflight.
- **Fix:** host the app on the same instance. For a package that is also mirrored to GitHub, use the reusable workflow at `.github/workflows/php-package.yml` in this repo instead of the components.
- **Check:** the include path starts with `$CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/`, and the app's project is on that same instance.

#### The components do not run on merge requests[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-components-do-not-run-on-merge-requests)

The components are ordinary jobs, so they run whenever the app's pipeline runs. Whether the pipeline runs on a merge request is decided by a `workflow:rules` block, and a component cannot set it for the project that includes it.

- **Cause:** the app's own `.gitlab-ci.yml` has no `workflow:rules` block with a `merge_request_event` rule.
- **Fix:** add the block to the app's own file:

```yaml
workflow:
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"
    - if: $CI_COMMIT_BRANCH == $CI_DEFAULT_BRANCH
```

- **Check:** a merge request pipeline runs, and so does a push to the default branch.

#### A gate was skipped or weakened[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#a-gate-was-skipped-or-weakened)

An included component is a set of ordinary jobs. The app's own `.gitlab-ci.yml` is merged over them, so an app can override a job's keys, skip it with `rules`, or delete the `include:` line. Preflight makes the safe pipeline the easy one. It does not lock it.

- **Cause:** a change in the app's own `.gitlab-ci.yml` overrides, skips or removes a component job.
- **Fix:** review the diff of the app's `.gitlab-ci.yml` against the last known-good pipeline, and restore the job or the `include:` line.
- **Check:** Rollcall is where skipped or weakened gates show up.

#### Two includes of the same component became one job[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#two-includes-of-the-same-component-became-one-job)

Every component except `portability` takes a `job_name` input, whose default is the job's usual name. Without it, two includes of the same component share a job name and merge into one.

- **Cause:** one project includes the same component more than once (for example in a monorepo with two apps) without setting `job_name`.
- **Fix:** set `job_name` on each include, for example `pint-app` and `pint-admin`. `job_name` ships in 0.1.4, so pin 0.1.4 or a SHA at or after that release.
- **Check:** the pipeline lists one job per include, with the names you set.

#### A fork merge request ran with protected variables[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#a-fork-merge-request-ran-with-protected-variables)

A fork's merge request pipeline runs the fork's configuration.

- **Cause:** the project lets fork pipelines see protected variables.
- **Fix:** review a fork's `.gitlab-ci.yml` before running its pipeline, and never give it protected variables.
- **Check:** the fork pipeline's variable list does not include any protected variable.

### Job failures[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#job-failures)

#### PROCTOR's preflight-pinned check warns[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#proctor-s-preflight-pinned-check-warns)

A tag or branch can move. A SHA cannot. PROCTOR's `preflight-pinned` check warns when an include is not pinned to a commit SHA.

- **Cause:** the include is pinned to a tag or a branch instead of a full commit SHA.
- **Fix:** pin the full commit SHA and keep the tag in a trailing comment, as in the examples on the [Components](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/components.html) page.
- **Check:** PROCTOR's report no longer carries the `preflight-pinned` finding.

#### composer-audit is green, then an advisory lands[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#composer-audit-is-green-then-an-advisory-lands)

New advisories are published after code is merged, so a green pipeline today can be stale tomorrow.

- **Cause:** no pipeline has run since the advisory was published.
- **Fix:** create a weekly pipeline schedule on the default branch: project settings, Build, Pipeline schedules. The component needs nothing extra. It carries no `rules:` block, so it runs in scheduled pipelines like any other. Someone with Maintainer rights on the app creates the schedule.
- **Check:** the schedule appears under project settings, Build, Pipeline schedules, and its latest pipeline is green.

#### php-test-next is red[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#php-test-next-is-red)

A red `php-test-next` job is an early warning, not a stop. It is the second `php-test` include that tries the PHP release that is not supported yet, with `allow_failure: true` in the app's own file.

- **Cause:** the next PHP release still fails the app's tests, or only has release candidate images.
- **Fix:** leave `allow_failure: true` in place while the release is unsupported. Once the release is supported (the supported versions follow `policy.json`), drop the `allow_failure` and move the version into the main `php_versions` list.
- **Check:** the main `php-test` matrix is green. Only the named `php-test-next` job is red.

#### package-publish refuses the tag[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#package-publish-refuses-the-tag)

The job reads the registry before publishing. Republishing a version from the same commit is a no-op, and republishing it from a different commit fails instead of overwriting the version, because GitLab would otherwise overwrite it without a word.

- **Cause:** the tag's version already exists in the group's Composer registry, published from a different commit.
- **Fix:** publish a new version tag instead of moving the old one. Protect the release tags so only maintainers can create or move a tag.
- **Check:** the job log shows the version already on the manifest and the commit it was published from.

#### portability is not in the pinned ref[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#portability-is-not-in-the-pinned-ref)

Portability ships in 0.1.4 and later. 0.1.3 does not include it.

- **Cause:** the include is pinned to a tag or SHA at or before 0.1.3.
- **Fix:** pin the `0.1.4` tag, or the full commit SHA of a commit at or after it.
- **Check:** the pipeline lists `portability-build` and `portability-run`.

#### portability-build fails on the runner[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#portability-build-fails-on-the-runner)

The build job runs Buildah, which uses unshare for its storage.

- **Cause:** the runner does not permit user namespaces.
- **Fix:** run the build job on a runner that permits user namespaces. The job sets `STORAGE_DRIVER: vfs`, so it needs no special kernel support beyond that.
- **Check:** the job log shows an unshare failure before the fix, and a successful `buildah bud` after it.

#### portability-run's health check ends in EOF[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#portability-run-s-health-check-ends-in-eof)

goss sends the HTTP method as written, and a lower-case one makes the server close the connection, so the health check failed with EOF. The check now uses `method: GET`, fixed in 0.1.4.

- **Cause:** the include is pinned to a ref before 0.1.4, where the goss health check used a lower-case method.
- **Fix:** pin 0.1.4 or a SHA at or after it.
- **Check:** `goss validate` passes the health check instead of ending in EOF.

### Renovate[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#renovate)

#### Renovate sees literal text instead of a token[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#renovate-sees-literal-text-instead-of-a-token)

On GitLab 19.5 a self-reference such as `RENOVATE_TOKEN: $RENOVATE_TOKEN` in the job `variables:` arrives as literal text and shadows the masked project CI/CD variables. The component does not map either token on purpose. The job reads both straight from the project.

- **Cause:** the runner project, or the app's file, adds `RENOVATE_TOKEN: $RENOVATE_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_COM_TOKEN: $GITHUB_COM_TOKEN` to `variables:`.
- **Fix:** delete the self-reference. Keep `RENOVATE_TOKEN` (and optionally `GITHUB_COM_TOKEN`) as masked CI variables in the private runner project.
- **Check:** the job log no longer shows the literal text `$RENOVATE_TOKEN`, and Renovate authenticates.

#### Renovate auto-merged a component pin bump[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#renovate-auto-merged-a-component-pin-bump)

In refs before 0.1.4 the component-rule manager name in `renovate/default.json` did not match repository deps, so a bump of a `component:` include version auto-merged instead of waiting for review.

- **Cause:** the shared preset comes from a ref before the 0.1.4 fix.
- **Fix:** point the repositories' `renovate.json` at the shared preset from 0.1.4 or later. Component version bumps now carry the `needs-review` label and never auto-merge.
- **Check:** the merge request carries the `needs-review` label.

### Local checks[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#local-checks)

#### The portability fixtures fail on permissions[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#the-portability-fixtures-fail-on-permissions)

The app user is not the host user that owns the fixtures' temp dir, and goss is downloaded into it. As of 0.1.4 the fixtures make their temp dir mode 0777 and the goss files in it mode 0644.

- **Cause:** the checkout is from a ref before 0.1.4.
- **Fix:** update to 0.1.4 or later, then rerun `sh tests/check-portability.sh` (or the `.ps1` twin).
- **Check:** the script exits 0: `good` passes and both `bad-*` fixtures fail.

#### composer ci fails on a stale docs site[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#composer-ci-fails-on-a-stale-docs-site)

`composer ci` runs `docs:check`, which fails when the built docs site is stale or the generated command or environment reference has drifted from the CLI or source.

- **Cause:** a page under `docs/` (or a generated reference) changed without rebuilding `site/docs/`.
- **Fix:** run `composer docs` to rebuild `site/docs/` from `docs/`, and commit the rebuilt site with the page.
- **Check:** `composer docs:check` passes.

### Related[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.html#related)

- [What the components cannot force](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/what-components-cannot-force.html)
- [Same instance only](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/same-instance-only.html)
- [Include a component twice](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/include-twice.html)
- [Renovate](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/renovate.html)

Source: https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html

## Upgrading[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#upgrading)

This page is the checklist for moving an app from one Preflight pin to the next, one released version at a time, newest first; every section follows `CHANGELOG.md`. Read the section for the version you are moving to, apply its steps, and verify on the next pipeline. Like a real preflight, the walk takes a few minutes and earns its keep: move the pin only after you have read the version notes.

### Unreleased[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#unreleased)

#### Changed[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#changed)

The `portability` component's `buildah_image` default moved from the plain version tag to the immutable tag `quay.io/buildah/stable:v1.43.5-immutable@sha256:7c2b605262748ace2c5c57c5550942d0adad57aec82ede3070927722306c0ffb`: Red Hat re-pushed the plain version tag and garbage-collected the old digest, so a pipeline pinned to it broke. If your app overrides `buildah_image`, point it at an `-immutable` tag pinned by digest too.

### 0.1.4[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-4)

Released 2026-11-03. The new pieces are opt-in: the `portability` component, a `job_name` input on every component except `portability`, and a stricter Renovate preset.

#### Breaking[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#breaking)

0.1.4 has no breaking changes: the version adds a component, an input and preset rules, and removes nothing.

#### Deprecated[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#deprecated)

Nothing was deprecated in 0.1.4.

#### Steps[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps)

Point each component include at the `0.1.4` tag, pinned to the tag's full commit SHA with the tag in a trailing comment:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/proctor@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
```

A mirrored package pins the same SHA in its GitHub workflow:

```yaml
jobs:
  ci:
    uses: waynestate/preflight/.github/workflows/php-package.yml@79029cc2300702d0d450c42cc699e12af1b731f8 # 0.1.4
```

Adopt the new pieces when you want them:

- **`portability`**: it ships in 0.1.4 and later (0.1.3 does not include it), so pin the `0.1.4` tag, or the full commit SHA of a commit at or after it. The build job needs a runner that permits user namespaces (Buildah uses unshare for its storage); the run job needs only the project's container registry and an app image that carries curl, sha256sum and tar.
- **`job_name`**: it ships in 0.1.4, so pin 0.1.4 or a SHA at or after that release. Set it when one project includes the same component more than once, for example in a monorepo with two apps; without it the two jobs would share a name and merge into one.
- **Renovate preset**: component version bumps now really wait for review instead of auto-merging (the component-rule manager name is `gitlabci`, matching repository deps), and a bump of the recorded Squire kit version carries the `squire-kit` label and never auto-merges; a person runs `squire update` to refresh the kit files.

Note

Pins change only through a reviewed merge request. A tag or branch can move; a SHA cannot.

#### How to verify[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify)

Push the change and run the app's pipeline. The components are ordinary jobs, so they run whenever the app's pipeline runs; expect the same jobs as before, green. PROCTOR's `preflight-pinned` check warns when an include is not pinned to a commit SHA. If you added `portability`, the `portability-run` job passes only when the image boots the strict way and the goss checks hold.

### 0.1.3[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-3)

Released 2026-11-03. Two consumer-facing changes: the `proctor` component installs the app with `--no-plugins --no-scripts`, and the shared Renovate preset stopped auto-merging the pins that every pipeline runs.

#### Breaking[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#breaking-1)

0.1.3 has no breaking changes, but the `proctor` job now installs the app's dependencies with `composer install --no-plugins --no-scripts`, so the app's plugins and scripts never run inside the job.

#### Deprecated[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#deprecated-1)

Nothing was deprecated in 0.1.3.

#### Steps[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps-1)

Bump each component include to the `0.1.3` tag's full commit SHA, with the tag in a trailing comment:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/proctor@<full commit SHA> # 0.1.3
```

If your group runs the shared Renovate preset, read the two behavior changes before you merge the bump:

- Updates inside `templates/**`, `contract/**` and `.gitlab-ci.yml`, and bumps of a Preflight component version in an app's `component:` include, no longer auto-merge: they carry the `needs-review` label and wait for a person.
- The `renovate` component no longer sets `RENOVATE_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_COM_TOKEN` from themselves in the job `variables:`; on GitLab 19.5 that self-reference arrived as literal text and shadowed the masked project CI/CD variables, so the job now reads both tokens straight from the project.

Warning

Do not add `RENOVATE_TOKEN: $RENOVATE_TOKEN` to your own `variables:`; that self-reference arrives as literal text.

#### How to verify[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify-1)

Run the pipeline and confirm the jobs run on the new pin. In the runner project, confirm the job reads `RENOVATE_TOKEN` straight from the project as a masked CI variable, and that a bump touching the templates, the contract or a component include pin opens a merge request labeled `needs-review` instead of auto-merging.

### 0.1.2[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-2)

Released 2026-10-29. The site gained the agent-ready kit (prompt blocks, Markdown twins, llms.txt) from Squire, and the proof page moved to a private site that needs a Wayne State sign-in.

#### Breaking[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#breaking-2)

0.1.2 has no breaking changes: the version touches the site, the README and the proof page, not the components.

#### Deprecated[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#deprecated-2)

Nothing was deprecated in 0.1.2.

#### Steps[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps-2)

Bump each component include to the `0.1.2` tag's full commit SHA, with the tag in a trailing comment:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/proctor@<full commit SHA> # 0.1.2
```

#### How to verify[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify-2)

Run the pipeline and confirm the component jobs run on the new pin. PROCTOR's `preflight-pinned` check warns when an include is not pinned to a commit SHA.

### 0.1.1[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-1)

Released 2026-10-29. Two new components: `package-publish`, which publishes a semantic version tag to the GitLab group's built-in Composer registry, and `renovate`, with the shared preset `renovate/default.json`. The reusable GitHub Actions workflow for mirrors ships in this tag too.

#### Breaking[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#breaking-3)

0.1.1 has no breaking changes: the version adds components and changes only the repository's own PHPStan config.

#### Deprecated[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#deprecated-3)

Nothing was deprecated in 0.1.1.

#### Steps[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps-3)

Bump the existing includes to the `0.1.1` tag's full commit SHA, and add the new components where you want them:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/package-publish@<full commit SHA> # 0.1.1
    inputs:
      group_id: "<your group id>"
```

`group_id` is required: the numeric id of the GitLab group whose built-in Composer registry hosts the package.

Warning

Protect your release tags. A component ref is a tag, so whoever can move it controls every pipeline that pins it.

A package mirrored to GitHub calls the reusable workflow from its own `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; the workflow ships in the `0.1.1` tag, so pin the full commit SHA of the release tag and keep the tag in a trailing comment:

```yaml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: ['**']
    tags: ['v*', '*.*.*']

jobs:
  ci:
    uses: waynestate/preflight/.github/workflows/php-package.yml@<full commit SHA> # 0.1.1
```

#### How to verify[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify-3)

Run the pipeline. For `package-publish`, the job runs only on tags and reads the registry first: a version already published from this commit passes quietly, and a version published from a different commit fails the pipeline. For a mirrored package, a release tag is not done until it is green on both sides.

### 0.1.0[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#0-1-0)

Released 2026-10-27. First tagged release.

#### Breaking[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#breaking-4)

0.1.0 is the first tagged release, so there is nothing to break: it is the baseline every later pin moves from.

#### Deprecated[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#deprecated-4)

Nothing was deprecated in 0.1.0.

#### Steps[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#steps-4)

Include the components pinned to the `0.1.0` tag's full commit SHA:

```yaml
include:
  - component: $CI_SERVER_FQDN/enterprise-apps/preflight/proctor@<full commit SHA> # 0.1.0
```

#### How to verify[#](https://preflight.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.html#how-to-verify-4)

Run the pipeline and confirm the component jobs run on the pin.
